name: Abide Christian Fellowship
description: Abide Christian Fellowship is a fellowship at Stanford of both graduates and undergraduates that take the Bible seriously. We meet every week to study the Bible, have fun, talk about life, and build lasting friendships.

name: Afghan Student Union
description: The mission of the Afghan Student Union (ASU) is to create a supportive and inclusive community for Afghan students at Stanford University, while promoting Afghan culture and raising awareness about the challenges faced by Afghan communities, particularly in light of the current geopolitical crisis. Our organization seeks to create a supportive community while advocating for educational opportunities, especially for women in Afghanistan. Through outreach, advocacy, and solidarity, ASU strives to strengthen the voice of the Afghan diaspora and foster understanding among diverse communities at S

name: Akwaaba Ghanaian Students Association
description: Akwaaba fosters unity, friendship, and solidarity among the Ghanaian community on campus through regular engagement with the Ghanaian, African, and Black communities at Stanford.

name: Alcohol Intolerance and Cancer Awareness Project
description: The Stanford chapter of the Alcohol Intolerance & Cancer Awareness Project (AICAP) promotes education, prevention, and research on alcohol intolerance and its established association with increased cancer risk, with particular focus on the often-misunderstood “Asian flush” response. Through campus-wide outreach, collaborative programming, and faculty-guided research partnerships with Stanford Medicine, AICAP provides evidence-based health education that empowers students to make informed decisions and supports early intervention around an underestimated public health issue.

name: Alexander Hamilton Society
description: The Alexander Hamilton Society is an independent, non-partisan, not-for-profit organization dedicated to promoting constructive debate on contemporary issues in foreign, economic, and national security policy.

name: Alliance
description: Founded in 1998, Alliance is a choreography-based dance team, driven by ambition, inspired by dance, and grounded in a love for our community. Our members come from a variety of backgrounds, ranging from classical ballet to hip hop to cultural dance, and this diversity of experiences is reflected in our choreography. In addition to hosting open workshops with local and professional industry dancers, we also perform at numerous on-campus events, including Pre-Audition Workshop, Alumni Homecoming, Breaking Ground, Winter Performing Arts Festival, ECC, Admit Weekend and, of course, our spring sho

name: Alpha Kappa Psi
description: Alpha Kappa Psi is a professional co-ed business fraternity that seeks to develop its members into principled business leaders and develop a strong community of like-minded business individuals.
policyNote: Professional fraternity — open to all genders. Membership is by application and interview.

name: Alternative Spring Break
description: Alternative Spring Breaks @ Stanford Service. Learning. Social Change. Alternative Spring Breaks (ASB) @ Stanford are immersive service-learning programs that expose students to pressing social and cultural issues through community engagement, experiential education, direct service, group discussions, assigned readings, and reflective activities. The program’s vision is to empower students to become informed advocates for social change—locally, nationally, and globally. ASB is a student-led Voluntary Student Organization (VSO) at Stanford University and an affiliate of the Haas Center for Publ

name: American Indian Science and Engineering Society
description: We aim to substantially increase the representation of American Indian and Alaskan Native students in engineering, science and other related technology disciplines by promoting a learning atmosphere that encourages professionalism and academic success.

name: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics
description: The mission of this student branch is to further, within Stanford, the purposes and programs of AIAA. Additionally, the student branch is established to highlight to Stanford and the local community the value of the aerospace industry and the role played by AIAA.

name: Animal Service Project
description: The Animal Service Project (ASP) is dedicated to supporting in-need and often underfunded animal welfare organizations through meaningful volunteer service and community partnership; we believe that caring for animals also means caring for the people and environments that depend on them. By connecting students with hands-on opportunities in shelters, rescues, sanctuaries, and wildlife organizations, ASP works to improve animal well-being while strengthening the communities and ecosystems they are part of. Our mission is to foster compassion, responsibility, and mutual benefit for animals, peop

name: Anime in the Arts
description: The purpose of our organization is to bring joy and light to campus through the celebration and active exploration of Japanese animation through photography and art. We move to build a creative community that emphasizes Japanese culture in the context of anime.

name: Arab Student Association at Stanford
description: The Arab Students Association at Stanford (ASAS) is a platform for Arab students that fosters social, academic, and extracurricular activities. It is time for the Arabs at Stanford to meet and get to know each other, in order to make a difference on campus!

name: Arbor Live
description: Stanford's student-run production company

name: Argentinos en Stanford
description: Our mission is to promote the knowledge of Argentine culture among the Stanford community through cultural, social and recreational events.

name: Armenian Students Association
description: The Armenian Students Assocation (ASA) is an association of undergraduate and graduate students with an interest in Armenian culture. We welcome all students who express an interest in Armenian issues and the ASA.

name: ArtX
description: To cultivate and sustain a community for those interested in bridging their interests in the arts in an effort to bridge the divides between diverse departments which exist on Stanford's campus and cultivate a central space for creativity.

name: ASES: Stanford's Global Entrepreneurship Society
description: ASES is a global student organization dedicated to connecting Stanford students with entrepreneurs and industry leaders throughout the world. ASES facilitates mentoring, conferences, networking, and educational opportunities based around entrepreneurship globally.

name: Asha for Education- Stanford Chapter
description: Asha Stanford's mission is promoting education projects that are specific to establishing sustainable education practices in India. We do this by funding several educational projects. On campus we hold events like Holi (in Spring) and plan on holding a brand new Garba event in the Fall!

name: Asian American Students' Association
description: Serving the Asian and Asian American Community at Stanford through education, organization, service, and action.

name: Asian American Theater Project
description: The Asian American Theater Project is dedicated to cultivating a space that empowers artists and audiences to engage with issues affecting the API community (including, but not limited to, discussions of identity, race, and representation), facilitate discussions of these issues within the larger Stanford community, and participate in the imagination and creation of a more equitable, just world through the language of theater.

name: Asian Cultural Exchange
description: The mission of Asian Cultural Exchange (ACE) is to build a more connected Stanford community through inclusive social spaces and shared cultural experiences. We bring students together across backgrounds to form genuine friendships through food, games, and tradition. ACE offers a space to celebrate all Asian cultures, fostering openness and new friendships.

name: Asian Pacific American Medical Student Association
description: ALMMA promotes mental health awareness and culturally responsive programming for immigrant communities in the Bay Area. Through direct service to immigrant youth and intergroup solidarity initiatives, ALMMA fosters cross-cultural understanding and equips Stanford students to engage as allies in community-based mental health work.

name: Asian Women's Alliance
description: The Asian Women's Alliance exists to provide a space for Asian and Asian-American women and allies to gather in solidarity with one another and deepen our understanding of ethnic identity while creating lasting bonds.

name: Associated Students of Stanford University (ASSU)
description: The Associated Students of Stanford University was created in 1891 and is the only organization at Stanford of which every student is a member. The ASSU provides funding to over five hundred volunteer student organizations (VSO). These organizations in turn provide the majority of cultural, political, recreational and religious programming for the entire campus. The financial independence that the ASSU affords student organizations is one of the founding principles of the organization. The ASSU also works to represent the interests, needs and perspectives of Stanford students at every level of

name: Association of Chinese Students and Scholars at Stanford
description: The Association of Chinese Students and Scholars at Stanford (ACSSS) is a student organization founded in 1989 and officially registered at Stanford University. We adhere to the concept of "connecting China and the United States and promoting exchanges," and serve the life, study, and career of Chinese students and scholars in Stanford and surrounding areas.

name: Association of Computing Machinery
description: The Chapter is organized and will be operated exclusively for educational and scientific purposes to promote the following: 1. An increased knowledge of and greater interest in the science, design, development, construction, languages, management and applications of modern computing. 2. Greater interest in computing and its applications. 3. A means of communication between persons having an interest in computing.

name: Association of Graduate Student Veterans
description: AGSV will serve as the primary student organization supporting community for student Veterans who are pursuing their non-professional graduate degrees (Masters and PhD). AGSV will work in tandem with SUAV to provide resources to students that are both actively serving or transitioning careers.

name: Association of Women Surgeons - Stanford Med Chapter
description: To empower and support female medical students pursuing surgical careers by providing mentorship, educational resources, and a collaborative community, thereby promoting diversity, equity, and excellence in the field of surgery.

name: Asylum Collaborative at Stanford Medicine
description: To provide comprehensive medical and psychological evaluations to asylum-seekers across the Bay Area.

name: Australia and New Zealand Club
description: The goal of the club is to foster community with Australian and New Zealander's on campus (as well as alumni) through social events and opportunities.

name: Awareness, Listening, Mental Health for iMmigrants and Allies
description: ALMMA promotes mental health awareness and culturally responsive programming for immigrant communities in the Bay Area. Through direct service to immigrant youth and intergroup solidarity initiatives, ALMMA fosters cross-cultural understanding and equips Stanford students to engage as allies in community-based mental health work.

name: Azerbaijani Student Association
description: Our mission is to introduce Azerbaijani culture to other students. celebrate and share Azerbaijani culture at Stanford by creating a welcoming community, hosting cultural events, and building cross-cultural connections through art, food, music, history, and dialogue.

name: Bahai Association at Stanford
description: The purpose of the Baha'i Association at Stanford is to promote the unity of mankind; to foster love and fellowship; to invite those interested to meaningfully discuss and explore both the teachings of the Baha'i Faith and their application to their lives; to organize activities that nurture collective and individual spiritual growth; and to be of service to the Stanford community and beyond.

name: Ballet Folklorico de Stanford
description: The purpose of this organization is to provide a cultural and educational experience for the Stanford campus community and the surrounding communities by exposing them to the tradition of Mexican folkloric dance.

name: Bangladeshi Students Association of Stanford
description: To celebrate our collective identity, embrace and serve our community, and create a safe space for all Bangali, Bangladeshi, and allied members of the Stanford community.

name: Barrio Assistance
description: The Barrio Assistance Tutoring Program exists to provide consistent and quality academic tutoring and mentoring for K-12 school children in the community, primarily from East Palo Alto and Menlo Park. The program focuses on providing individualized tutoring to each child, given their academic and language needs. We aim to provide our students with a holistic approach to programming—one that engages them academically while also enriching them as full and complex persons. In this way, it is our mission to assist our students in developing positive self-images, self-learning, and self pride, in a

name: Basmati Raas
description: Basmati Raas is Stanford's only Garba Raas dance team and one of few nationally competitive dance groups on campus. We have been a prominent member of Stanford's student life since our creation in 2012. Our mission is to share our love of dance and Indian culture with the Stanford community.

name: BioJam CoLABS
description: Our mission is to engage teens through their own creativity and culture in bioengineering/biomaterial design and create pathways for them to share their learning in their home communities.

name: Biological Interdisciplinary Open Maker Environment
description: BIOME is a student organization dedicated to providing open space for anyone interested in pursuing bioengineering and biology inspired projects. Our mission is to provide any Stanford student with the skills, resources, and support to engage in a bio-hacking project. Bio-hacking includes any project that utilizes biological materials. We seek to educate our membership and the broader public and strive to broaden the scope of biotechnology beyond the conventional definition.

name: Biomedical Association for the Interest for Minority Students
description: The Biomedical Association for the Interest of Minority Students (BioAIMS) is an inclusive organization that provides a welcoming home for all Biosciences students at Stanford to celebrate their identities--especially those that have traditionally been marginalized in academia. We actively build this community through cultural celebrations, peer support, and career development programming. To address the issues facing our communities, we engage in social justice advocacy and local outreach initiatives.

name: Black Creative Collective
description: The Black Creative Collective is a student-initiated and run organization dedicated to promoting a collaborative and shared artistic community for Black students of African descent at Stanford. Through interdisciplinary projects, workshops, and showcases, we create a space for Black creatives across mediums–such as film, music, visual arts, fashion, and more–to connect, share, and amplify their work. In a campus arts culture where Black artists often feel underrepresented, the work of BCC ensures that Black creativity is celebrated and shared amongst the community. Our mission is to curate a t

name: Black Engineering Graduate Student Association
description: BEGSA's mission is to build a sense of community among and facilitate the professional development and academic success of the Black Stanford engineering community by providing forums for engagement, discussion, and collective learning.

name: Black Family Gathering Committee
description: Our organization's mission is to create space meant to center and uplift the black communities on both our campus and within the broader Bay Area

name: Black Graduate Students Association
description: The members of the Black Graduate Student Association (BGSA) of Stanford University, for the sake of the intellectual, social, and cultural enrichment of the Black graduate students and the broader Stanford community, pledge to envision and construct a thriving community characterized by joy, freedom, and intellectual curiosity. We will leverage our access to institutional resources to strengthen our communities and address the social, economic, environmental, and political barriers that we face.

name: Black Oceans Stanford Scholars
description: Our main goal is to support Black graduate students and post-docs in the Oceans field here at Stanford in order to create community, aid in retention, and expand our network of resources and mentors within Stanford and beyond.

name: Black Pre-Law Society
description: The Mission of The Black Pre-Law Society is to promote the vitality of students interested in pursuing careers in law within Stanford's black community. The club will attempt, to the best of its members interests and resources, mitigate the issues black lawyers face when practicing law. In doing so, The Black Pre-Law Society hopes to serve as a resource and vibrant hub that allows for Stanford's black pre-law students and ally's to connect with each other and develop the foundation to lead or create successful companies in the future.

name: Black Rhythm and Sound
description: We are a community of creatives capturing and reimagining Black entertainment and Hip Hop spaces. Through unparalleled events, mentorship, and networking opportunities, we pride ourselves on creating synergetic spaces for bonding, personal growth, and career acceleration centered around Blackness and Black entertainment.

name: Blackstage
description: Stanford BLACKstage aims to tell stories of marginalized communities not often represented in traditional theater, primarily from the black perspective. The purpose of BLACKstage is to provide high caliber performance and creative opportunities for all students, as well as tell the stories of marginalized communities not often represented in traditional theater, primarily centered around the Black perspective. BLACKstage is a space for performers, artists, musicians, designers, and other creatives to showcase their talents and create a collective effort towards socially conscious storytelling.

name: Body Empowerment Project
description: Body Empowerment Project seeks to empower people to find body acceptance and self-worth. We work to prevent eating disorders, specifically in populations that lack access to treatment, representation, and preventive care. Our primary goal is to raise eating disorder awareness and provide preventative resources within the SMS community.

name: Brazilian Students Association
description: Promote the richness of the Brazilian culture, history, and language, while bringing together and supporting both Brazilians and interested non-Brazilians at Stanford.

name: Bridges International
description: Bridges International is an organization which focuses on helping international students and their families thrive by providing supportive relationships, activities, cultural experiences, tours around the Bay Area, Bible studies, Christian mentoring, and opportunities to get involved in community service outreaches.

name: Buddhist Community at Stanford
description: The Buddhist Community At Stanford supports members of the Stanford community who are interested in engaging with Buddhism and practicing Buddhist meditation and other practices. BCAS provides opportunities on campus for everyone, regardless of religious affiliation and prior experience or knowledge, to engage with and learn more about what the many Buddhist traditions have to offer.

name: Business Association of Stanford Entrepreneurial Students
description: BASES is a student organization that seeks to empower the next generation of entrepreneurs through educational programming. We make entrepreneurial engagement accessible to the Stanford community, serving as a portal to Silicon Valley and beyond.

name: Caesura Journal
description: As Stanford's only undergraduate academic research journal focusing on the study of literature, Caesura strives to consistently spotlight the most current and insightful research conducted at the undergraduate level. Each edition features scholarly and creative pieces that aim to provoke new ways of thinking about literature. In giving voice to a diverse range of perspectives, Caesura provides an inclusive outlet for undergraduates to share their ideas and enrich the humanities community at Stanford.

name: Cambodian Student Association
description: Cambodian Student Association at Stanford University Mission Statement At CamSA, we build a community where members can be at home, foster meaningful relationships, and celebrate each other. We work together to preserve and maintain Cambodian traditions, cultures, and histories through advocacy work, community service, and mentorship. CamSA is a legacy and a future where members can explore issues in our communities and look towards liberatory possibilities together.

name: Canadian Student Organization
description: The Canadian Student Organization (CSO) is a non-political volunteer student organization committed to fostering a welcoming and inclusive environment for all its members, respecting their diverse backgrounds and cultural identities. Our primary objective is to organize and sponsor social and cultural activities and events that celebrate the rich tapestry of Canadian heritage among the Canadian community at Stanford, welcoming all those interested in anything related to Canada to engage with us and one another. We aim to promote a deeper understanding of Canadian culture, create opportunities

name: Cap and Gown
description: The mission of Cap and Gown is to cultivate and empower women leaders by bringing together members of the Stanford community who demonstrate and celebrate women's leadership. We connect active women leaders on campus to our successful alumni through meaningful service and networking events. With over 2,000 alumni in a variety of fields, Cap and Gown promotes women's leadership across the world.

name: Cardinal Ballet Company
description: Cardinal Ballet Company (CBC) is Stanford's first and only ballet company. Founded in 1993 and completely student-run, CBC is composed of dancers from diverse backgrounds, including those with professional ballet and contemporary training. In addition to our 2 major ballet productions every year (the Nutcracker in the fall and a full-length ballet in the spring), we also offer opportunities for student choreography in various dance forms. Our mission is to bring dancers together who love performing and share our art with the community.

name: Cardinal Calypso
description: Cardinal Calypso is Stanford University's premiere steelpan ensemble. We bring the music and culture of Trinidad and Tobago to the greater university community by performing both traditional Caribbean music and popular songs.

name: Cardinal Free Clinics
description: The mission of Cardinal Free Clinics is to provide culturally appropriate, high quality transitional medical care for an underserved patient population and to educate and empower a new generation of health care leaders to proactively address health disparities and improve access to care in their communities.

name: Cardinal Policy Group
description: The Cardinal Policy Group provides students with an opportunity to develop skills relevant to policy analysis and work with policymakers and organizations to use policy as a lever for social change.

name: Cardinal Tap Dance
description: Cardinal Tap Dance aims to cultivate Stanford’s tap dance community by providing a space for dancers of different levels to practice, build their skills, and carry on tap dance tradition and culture.

name: Cardinal West Coast Swing
description: The purposes of the club are to promote West Coast Swing (WCS), to support WCS dancers and to grow the WCS community at Stanford.

name: Cards 4 Kids
description: We are Cards 4 Kids, an organization dedicated to fostering genuine connections, creating moments of joy, and building a supportive community for children through interactive, fun, and accessible sports-inspired activities.

name: Caribbean Students Association
description: CSA brings together students with Caribbean roots (by birth or descent) and students who wish to gain a greater understanding of Caribbean culture. We strive to foster social culture, political, and academic awareness around Caribbean culture and topical issues.

name: Catholic Undergraduate Student Association
description: The Catholic Undergraduate Student Association is a family of students with Christ at the center. Through a variety of liturgical, social, educational, and community service programs, we seek to form the Christian conscience, help members engage with the Catholic faith, educate for justice, facilitate personal development, and form Catholic leaders for the future. We support the University's efforts to achieve its goals in keeping with our own traditions and in an environment of religious and cultural diversity.

name: Central American Student Association
description: We create this space to help navigate the Central American erasure in the Latino community at Stanford. It is important to recognize the diversity within the Central American diaspora. CASA is a space for CentAm's of all races, ethnicities, LGBTQ+ identity, religion, abilities, and/or immigration status. As we create this space we want to stress our commitment to Black/Indigenous folks within CentAm diaspora– who are too often at the forefront of the trauma in our community. This will be a continuous conversation at CASA as well as unpacking mestizaje and whiteness in LatAm/CentAm.

name: Central Asian Student Association
description: In recognition of the unique challenges faced by international students, especially those from Central Asia, our organization is dedicated to creating a nurturing environment at Stanford. We aim to establish a close-knit community where Central Asian students and their friends can find a sense of belonging, support, and camaraderie. Through a variety of inclusive activities and initiatives, we strive to enhance the overall student experience, providing a home away from home and fostering lasting connections that extend beyond the academic realm. name: Ceramics Club
description: We are a student-run organization at Stanford University offering studio membership and classes to the Stanford community.

name: Challah for Hunger
description: Stanford Challah builds community through baking and social advocacy. Through the communal act of baking, we aim to create a cooperative, interfaith space on campus, uniting diverse groups in a welcoming and accessible environment. Our goal is not only to support social justice non-profits, but more importantly to bring people together and be a catalyst for both international and local social change.

name: Chemical Engineering Graduate Students
description: We represent the academic, professional and social interests of graduate students in the Chemical Engineering department and provide help and support to both early and late career graduate students through specifically tailored events. We also promote the sense of community in the Chemical Engineering Department through social events!

name: Chicano Latino Graduate Student Association
description: Our mission is to create a sense and belonging a community among the Chicano/a/x Latino/a/x graduate student community.

name: Christian Union
description: The mission of Christian Union is to provide a space for Stanford students to explore their Christian faith through thoughtful conversations and cultivate their leadership skills through campus and community involvement.

name: Code the Change
description: We are a collective of STEM students and workers fighting for science and tech for liberation, not global oppression. The tech empire, with Stanford at its core, drives worker exploitation, surveillance, climate destruction, and genocidal violence. The system relies on our labor and complicity, and we have the power to halt this. Born from the Palestine solidarity movement, Tech for Liberation builds power in our departments, labs, and classrooms to end the tech war machine.

name: Colombian Student Association
description: The Colombian Students Association at Stanford aims to: - Promote the knowledge of Colombian culture among the Stanford community; - Organize and support cultural, social and recreational events for the Colombian students at Stanford and those interested in Colombia; - Provide information to prospective Colombian students; - Encourage the exchange of ideas about issues related to Colombia.

name: Common Origins
description: Common Origins is a dance group founded on the belief that everyone has the potential to be great – they simply need the opportunity to take that first step. Common Origins aims to foster a welcoming community for dancers of all backgrounds and identities. Though we are a dance team, it is our community that is most important to us. We hope for all our members to find a home on our team and to form long-lasting friendships. As a non-audition group, we welcome dancers of all levels, at any time, to join us. We aim to challenge and train our members with fresh, exciting choreography that we perf

name: Community Emergency Response Team (Stanford)
description: To promote emergency preparedness on campus and organize a campus Community Emergency Response Team which may be deployed by the Stanford Department of Public Safety.

name: Computer Science Student Council
description: This council aims to strengthen the CS community at Stanford, and enhance the experience of our university life. We serve CS students at Stanford in four aspects: academic, social, internal relations, and external relations.

name: Comunidad for Health Equity
description: CHE aims to create space for discussion on Latinx issues to support an interest in changing the fields of clinical and public health. We address the needs of our Latinx community by connecting members to volunteer opportunities while supporting them academically. We encourage an interdisciplinary education rooted in community service that addresses Latinx issues and those intersecting. We empower our community through mentorship within our organization and the medical school in order to build a larger network of resources while creating a sense of belonging. You do not have to be pre-med or La

name: Counterpoint a cappella
description: Counterpoint is Stanford's only soprano/alto a cappella group dedicated to making music, building a strong community of women through a shared love for singing, and developing our members' music skills and interests.

name: CS+Social Good
description: An organization of technologists, designers, and thinkers passionate about maximizing the benefits of technology and mitigating its harms. Showing students that there are a variety of ways to utilize their technical skills.

name: CSA Club Water Polo Team of Stanford
description: The purposes of this Club shall be to give Stanford students the opportunity to play organized, competitive water polo against other schools, to promote good health and physical fitness, and to foster team camaraderie and school spirit.

name: CSA JKA Shotokan of Stanford
description: Shotokan Karate is a weaponless martial art developed in Okinawa and Japan that emphasizes power and efficiency in combat. Skilled karateka defeat their opponents with a minimal number of techniques and effort, which is particularly useful when facing multiple opponents. JKA Shotokan is distinguished from other martial arts by the linearity and strength of its punches, blocks, and kicks. Precise techniques, accompanied by mastery and focus of energy flows and a deep knowledge of the body's vital points, make this karate style a comprehensive system for self-defense and combat. name: CSA Jugger at Stanford
description: To practice and promote jugger, the foam-fighting field sport.

name: CSA Men's Club Basketball
description: To continue the competitive basketball careers and associated positive impacts of competitive sports for Stanford undergraduate and graduate students through peer-to-peer competition, competition with fellow club basketball organizations, and camaraderie between teammates.

name: CSA Stanford Archery Club
description: To share our love for archery, to compete as a team, and to teach and improve our archery skills.

name: CSA Stanford Badminton Club
description: To provide a platform where people that enjoy badminton, regardless of their skill level, can come together and play.

name: CSA Stanford Boxing Club
description: The purpose of the Stanford Boxing Club is: to promote the sport of boxing among the student body; teach students how to box; provide opportunities to test student boxing skills in competition; and enhance the values of health, discipline, and community through boxing.

name: CSA Stanford Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Club
description: The Stanford Grappling and Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu club fosters an inclusive and friendly community in which students train submission grappling and ground fighting. Come join us for a fun and welcoming training session, no experience required!

name: CSA Stanford Climbing
description: The goal of Stanford Competitive Climbing Team is to create an all-inclusive community of people passionate or interested in improving their climbing skills by competing. Furthermore, the club seeks to create an environment of both encouragement, motivation, and learning to climbers of all different skill levels and backgrounds.

name: CSA Stanford Club Baseball
description: Stanford Club Baseball provides undergraduate and graduate students with an opportunity to play competitive baseball at the sub-varsity level. Through a mix of games and practices, it encourages experienced players to continue to develop their skills to maximize their contributions to the team. The club measures its success in terms of both its on-field production and the level of participation by its members. name: CSA Stanford Club Beach Volleyball
description: To create a space for the vibrant, diverse beach volleyball community on Stanford to come together through more formal training and gameplay with structured practices and competitions.

name: CSA Stanford Club Ice Hockey
description: Stanford Club Ice Hockey exists to give Stanford students a competitive, inclusive place to play the game they love. We are a competitive club team that offers an inclusive space for hockey players to get on the ice, sharpen their skills, and play against other universities around the West Coast, competing in the American Collegiate Hockey Association as a Division II team. We are run by and for our players, carrying forward a Stanford hockey tradition that traces back over a century.

name: CSA Stanford Club Sports
description: To provide instructional and recreational opportunities to Stanford undergraduate and graduate student-athletes in a player-oriented setting unique to the Club Sports program; To promote student-run athletic teams by emphasizing student leadership in training, competition, team management, and program direction; To encourage athletes at all levels, from recreational to elite, by maintaining a fun, athlete-focused environment and by recognizing individual and team achievement; To provide, where practical and appropriate, financial and logistical assistance to teams and athletes in advancing the

name: CSA Stanford Club Swimming
description: Provide fun and exciting workouts for all who want to swim at varying levels of competition.

name: CSA Stanford Club Tennis
description: Stanford Club Tennis is a selective, competitive co-ed tennis team comprised of Stanford undergraduate and graduate students. We are a member of the USTA NorCal Tennis on Campus Series and primarily compete against other Northern California club tennis teams. We placed 3rd in the 2017-18 National Championships and 2nd in last three Sectional Championships. We recently placed 9th in the 2022-23 National Championships. name: CSA Stanford Club Triathlon Team
description: We are a team based in the Stanford community, under the auspices of Stanford Club Sports, internally managed by team-elected, student officers. The team is open to all levels of ability and is comprised of 60+ athletes. Team members are working towards a wide range of individual as well as team goals.

name: CSA Stanford Cricket Club
description: Stanford Cricket Club aims to promote cricket on campus by providing both an inclusive community for students to learn, play, and enjoy the sport and a high-caliber club team to compete against other colleges. Through regular practices, competitive play, watch parties, and coaching sessions Stanford Cricket Club seeks to fill the gap in representation and foster a love for the world's second-most-played sport at Stanford.

name: CSA Stanford Cycling
description: Stanford Cycling welcomes all riders of any experience level in all cycling disciplines – if it has wheels and rolls we want you to bring it out! We firmly believe cycling is for everyone: whether you are interested in exploring, commuting, recreation, community, fitness, or racing, we want you to enjoy being on a bike. We are actively building an accepting and inclusive cycling environment and welcome individuals from all backgrounds.

name: CSA Stanford Dragon Boat
description: Encourage a welcoming community of dragon boat paddlers at Stanford!

name: CSA Stanford Equestrian Team
description: The Stanford Equestrian Team is a competitive organization dedicated to horsemanship, sportsmanship, education, leadership, teamwork, and intercollegiate equestrian competition. Members commit themselves to working cooperatively with teammates, coaches, and horses in both the barn and competition environments and to representing Stanford University with integrity, respect, and professionalism. The Team seeks to foster an inclusive and supportive environment that values personal growth, accountability, athletic achievement, and responsible stewardship of equine partners.

name: CSA Stanford Figure Skating Club
description: To create and nurture a competitive and recreational environment for Stanford students passionate about figure skating.

name: CSA Stanford Golf Club
description: Our goal is to make golf more accessible to Stanford students and create a community of passionate golfers at the Farm.

name: CSA Stanford Jump Rope
description: Stanford Jump Rope is a performance-based jump rope team that hosts workshops to the Stanford community and provides a space for students to get involved in fitness, performance, and competition through the sport of jump rope.

name: CSA Stanford Kendo Club
description: The Mission of the Stanford Kendo Club is to promote the safe practice of kendo on Stanford Campus, as well as to encourage respectful competition and the values of martial arts.

name: CSA Stanford Men's Club Soccer Team
description: To promote the love of the beautiful game of football (soccer), foster brotherhood, and build community on campus with a diverse group of players from all schools across Stanford.

name: CSA Stanford Men's Lacrosse
description: This group exists for members of the Stanford community to have the opportunity to play lacrosse in a competitive, team environment, regardless of past experience with the sport. The team competes in the Western Collegiate Lacrosse League (WCLL) of the Men's Collegiate Lacrosse Association (MCLA).

name: CSA Stanford Men's Rugby
description: Create opportunities for Stanford students to learn about themselves and the world through rugby

name: CSA Stanford Men's Ultimate Team
description: To provide every male Stanford student with the opportunity to learn and play ultimate frisbee. Our A-team offers the opportunity to compete at the highest levels of college ultimate, and our B-team allows players to opt for a lower level of commitment and competition while continuing to play the sport and enjoy the social aspects of being on a team.

name: CSA Stanford Men's Volleyball Club
description: Stanford Men's Volleyball Club strives to provide current Stanford students with equitable opportunity to participate in competitive, intercollegiate volleyball. We focus on engaging with each other as a tight knit team comprised of members representing many different parts of the student body in an effort to support one another both on and off the court.

name: CSA Stanford Muay Thai
description: Muay Thai is a form of Martial Arts that makes use of punches, elbows, kicks, and knees, as well as the clinch (stand-up grappling). The purpose of the Stanford Muay Thai Club Sport will be to provide Stanford students with 1. the opportunity to learn and safely practice Muay Thai techniques, 2. a fun and engaging way to improve mental/physical health through full-body training, 3. a tried-and-true method to develop discipline, confidence, and self-mastery, 4. a close-knit, supportive, and non-judgmental community.

name: CSA Stanford Pickleball Club
description: The purpose of the Stanford Pickleball Club is to provide a structured, welcoming, and inclusive pickleball community in which Stanford students of all levels of skill and interest can learn and play pickleball.

name: CSA Stanford Polo Club
description: The mission of the Stanford Polo Club is to provide an opportunity for Stanford students to learn to ride and play polo at a competitive, intercollegiate level. The Polo Club offers students the opportunity to learn about riding and polo, horse care and barn management, and it helps fulfill Stanford's goal of providing a truly broad education.

name: CSA Stanford Running Club
description: Welcoming runners of all levels, from casual to competitive :) Hosting daily runs from the Claw & track practices 2x/week. Competing @ local/regional/national cross-country & track meets!

name: CSA Stanford Ski Team
description: The mission of the Stanford Ski & Snowboard Club is to create a community of skiers and snowboarders, facilitate their access to the mountains, help them develop as athletes, offer regional and national collegiate competitions. We offer optional competitive teams for competition in United States Collegiate Ski and Snowboard Association races (NCAA Division II). Both skiers and snowboarders can participate in Racing, Park, and Freeride competitions.

name: CSA Stanford Squash Men's Intercollegiate Team
description: Stanford Club Squash, alongside the varsity women's team, represents Stanford in the College Squash Association as one of the league's top club programs. We play during the fall and winter quarters against both club and varsity teams across the country, including colleges like Cal, Brown, Navy, Northwestern and Notre Dame. And we travel! Many of our matches take place over weekend trips to places like New York, Boston and New Haven. We also host a West Coast tournament at our home courts in February, and wrap up each season at the National Championships, which take place at Harvard, Yale, or T

name: CSA Stanford Table Tennis Club
description: To play Table Tennis and compete in Table Tennis competitions.

name: CSA Stanford Taekwondo
description: Stanford Taekwondo is a club sport at Stanford University that provides high quality and professional taekwondo coaching for all skill levels. We offer avenues to develop skills for casual recreation, sparring, poomsae, coaching, and refereeing, as well as regular opportunities to compete nationally and train with international teams. All are welcome, from seasoned black belts to beginners who have never kicked before; at the heart of Stanford Taekwondo is a vibrant team that supports each other as both athletes and friends.

name: CSA Stanford Women's Club Lacrosse
description: Our team is dedicated to the sport and focuses on cohesion on and off the field. Our women continuously work to improve technical skills, expand game knowledge, and create a supportive and welcoming space for players of all experience levels.

name: CSA Stanford Women's Club Soccer
description: The Stanford Women's Club Soccer team aims to provide a space for female players to engage in the sport of soccer, build a lasting community, and have fun.

name: CSA Stanford Women's Club Volleyball
description: Provide a competitive volleyball program for Stanford women not able to practice varsity sports.

name: CSA Stanford Women's Rugby
description: The Stanford Women's Rugby Team, also known as SWR, was founded in 1977. Since its founding, the SWR program has produced All-Americans, USA National Team Players, and Olympic 7's Rugby National Team Players, and has won numerous National Championships. Today the team competes in intercollegiate competition in Olympic 7's Rugby in the fall, and 15's Rugby in the winter in the Pacific Mountain Conference. The Stanford Women's Rugby Team is consistently one of the top teams in the country and prides itself on upholding its key values of Resilience, Challenge, and Solidarity. With these values in

name: CSA Stanford Women's Ultimate
description: Mission: To play and promote the exciting game of Ultimate Frisbee. About our teams: We have two women's teams: Superfly (Women's A Team) and Firefly (Women's B Team). Superfly is more competitive and Firefly is more relaxed, but we do all of our activities together in the fall quarter, so you get to experience all of our programming and choose the level of involvement that floats your boat :] Are we any good? Yes! Our ultimate program has a long history of success. Stanford Superfly has been in the national championship finals fourteen times since 1995, with eight title wins– including 2016!–

name: CSA Stanford Women's Wrestling Club
description: The Stanford Women's Wrestling Club offers an inclusive opportunity for students of all genders and backgrounds to engage in collegiate-level wrestling. Whether pursuing the sport competitively or recreationally, this club serves as an accessible entry point to the great sport of wrestling. SWWC will cater to wrestlers (or wrestlers to be) of all experience and ability levels, including, most importantly, those without any prior wrestling experience.

name: CSA Stanford Wushu Club
description: To promote the awareness and the advancement of Chinese Martial Arts (wushu, tai chi, and sanshou) including its study, history, and culture through instruction, practice and competition.

name: CSA Women's Club Basketball
description: Stanford Women's Club Basketball aims to provide a fun environment for women who want to continue to play basketball competitively, but at a non-varsity level. We choose to have player coaches so that each member has a chance to exercise leadership on and off the court. Through practices, tournaments, and team dinners we strive to create our own separate community within the overall Stanford community.

name: Dancebreak
description: The goal of Dancebreak is to make social dance more accessible to Stanford University students. We seek to provide an opportunity for fun, casual social dancing which requires little to no previous experience of any dance form. We hold weekly workshops and practices and encourage experimentation in creating new Stanford-based dances. The purpose of Dancebreak is to build a community of social dance enthusiasts and share opportunities to learn, practice, perform, and enjoy social dance. We encourage dancers of all levels to interact and teach each other, and we provide opportunities for people

name: Derechos
description: We are Latine students interested in the law: ranging all the way from education and immigration to international relations and business. There is no undergraduate pre-law degree on the Stanford campus, so we provide a forum through which undergraduates can learn more about what the legal field and law school is like.

name: Dutch@Stanford
description: Dutch@Stanford provides opportunities those with an interest in the Netherlands or Dutch culture to convene, share and discuss this culture with others, and help acclimatize new Dutch students to Stanford University.

name: DV8
description: Stanford DV8 Hip-Hop Dance Group is a performance-based hip-hop dance group that performs for a wide variety of audiences. Whether teaching workshops or hosting our annual dance showcase 'Encounter Culture'—which features student and professional dance groups from across the Bay Area—DV8 promises to leave the crowd talking.

name: Earthquake Engineering Research Institute (EERI) Stanford Chapter
description: The EERI Stanford student chapter strives to provide students interested in structural and earthquake engineering with professional development and community-building opportunities. We organize events that promote interaction with industry, encourage research collaboration, and facilitate social connections. These include bringing speakers to campus, participating in outreach activities, and putting on social gatherings.

name: Earthtones
description: Earthtones is a student-led team that organizes and coordinates an annual environmental justice arts festival, called Earthtones. This festival takes place around Earth Day each year on the O'Donohue Family Stanford Educational Farm to celebrate the connection between people of color and the environment, uplifting those impacted by environmental injustices.

name: East African Stanford Students Association
description: Community building among East African students, faculty and friends of East Africa and giving Stanford students a taste of East African culture through music, language, food and history.

name: Educational Studies Program
description: The purpose of the Educational Studies Program is to provide extracurricular enrichment programs for secondary school students.

name: Engineering Students for Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
description: The purpose of this organization is to dismantle racism, sexism, ableism, homophobia, transphobia, classism, and ethnic discrimination and all forms of oppression in engineering departments, in solidarity with departments across Stanford and with other institutes of higher education. We aim to achieve this through nurturing and sustaining a diverse and inclusive community in the school of engineering via community-based programming such as book clubs, community socials, and faculty roundtables.

name: Engineers for a Sustainable World - Stanford Chapter
description: Founded in 2003, the Stanford chapter of Engineers for a Sustainable World (ESW) is a student-led affiliate of the Haas Center for Public Service. Stanford ESW aims to address the challenges of global poverty and sustainability by harnessing the energy and creativity of student engineers. We partner with organizations locally and internationally to approach engineering-based challenges through partnerships that foster cultural, educational, and technical exchange.

name: Everyday People
description: Everyday People (EP) was founded to uplift and honor the underrepresented voices of Black artists in the Stanford a capella scene and music more broadly. As a tribute to Sly and the Family Stone's vision of inclusiveness and acceptance of all races, genders, and creeds, our founders formed Everyday People, based on the group's 1967 hit of the same title. Today, EP continues to honor Sly and the Family Stone's mission to uplift and embrace music created by Black artists.

name: Faces of Afro Muslims
description: -To celebrate Black Muslim cultures and perspectives through events, programs, and educational initiatives that highlight the rich diversity within Black Muslim communities. -To create inclusive spaces that foster open dialogue, spiritual enrichment, and the free exploration of intersectional identities as Black and Muslim. -To advocate for greater representation, resources, and accommodation for Black Muslim students' specific cultural and religious needs.

name: FashionX
description: Stanford FashionX is the university's hub for any and all creatives interested in the fashion industry. Since our establishment in 2019, FashionX has been carving out a unique space for designers, technologists, and sustainability advocates alike to engage in fashion.

name: Fellowship of Christian Athletes in Action
description: The purpose of the club shall be to encourage, equip and empower student-athletes, coaches and all whom they influence to live out their faith freely within the athletic community and to grow and prosper in a relationship with Jesus Christ and using this relationship to positively impact others throughout campus. We believe that being a Christian is about having a personal relationship with God through Jesus Christ, and that true-life purpose and meaning can be found only in personal relationship with Jesus Christ.

name: First Love Stanford
description: First Love Church Stanford is committed to ministering the gospel through music, drama, skits, dancing and choreography, and other creative arts that help students use their talents in a meaningful way. We aim to foster deep connections and spiritual growth among students by creating a vibrant community centered around the regular sharing of the Word of God and building meaningful relationships. Through regular visits, intercessions, hangouts, and fellowship meetings, we aspire to enhance the spiritual, social, and emotional well-being of our members. We seek to exemplify love in all aspects o

name: Flamenco Cardenal
description: Flamenco Cardenal strives to cultivate artistic and intellectual community at Stanford centered on flamenco, an art form rooted in the musical traditions of the Romani diaspora, Latin America and the Caribbean, North and West Africa, and Spanish folkloric styles, many of which are of Islamic and Jewish origin. We hold flamenco classes for dancers, singers, and musicians, build relationships with the broader Bay Area flamenco community, organize group outings to local flamenco performances, and host academic lectures and workshops on critical and decolonial flamenco studies. In making Stanford

name: FLIP: First-Generation, Low-Income Partnership
description: The First-Generation and/or Low-Income Partnership is a volunteer student organization dedicated to supporting FLI students through building community, hosting workshops, fostering advocacy, and advancing conversations about socioeconomic class at Stanford and beyond. Join us and learn more!

name: Flying Horse Films
description: We want to bring together Stanford students interested in film production to create short films as a team. This will lead us to learn about the filmmaking process, exploring areas such as screenwriting, film production, direction, cinematography, editing, and more.

name: Flying Treehouse
description: Our mission is to cultivate and celebrate the imaginations and language arts of young people through creative writing workshops in local elementary schools, in-school performances of the young authors' stories, and a quarterly on-campus public performance of this work.

name: FreeFlow
description: FreeFlow is a freestyle dance club committed to creating an open and safe space for dancers of all experience levels to learn, cypher (freestyle dance jam where people take turns dancing within a circle), workshop, and express themselves. We want to make dance accessible for all students, and we are committed to understanding the roots, history, and cultures that various dance styles stem from. Each year, we support the broader dance communities and learn about the histories of freestyle dance by inviting guest artists and attending local Bay Area workshops/dance events. name: FSL African American Fraternal and Sororal Association
FSL Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated
description: Alpha Kappa Alpha's influence extends beyond campus quads and student interest. It has a legacy of service that deepens, rather than ends, with college graduation. The goals of its program activities center on significant issues in families, communities, government halls and world assembly chambers. Its efforts constitute a priceless part of the global experience in the 21st century

name: FSL Alpha Kappa Delta Phi
description: The sisterhood of alpha Kappa Delta Phi provides womxn with a sense of belonging that nurtures life-long friendships, develops self-empowered leaders, and strengthens communities through service, scholarship, and Asian-Awareness.

name: FSL Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc.
description: Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc. develops leaders, promotes brotherhood and academic excellence, while providing service and advocacy for our communities.

name: FSL Chi Omega
description: In the Nu Alpha chapter at Stanford, we are committed to our founding purposes: friendship, personal integrity, service to others, academic excellence and intellectual pursuits, community and campus involvement, and personal and career development. Chi Omega welcomes all individuals who identify as women into our sisterhood.

name: FSL Delta Kappa Epsilon Fraternity, Sigma Rho Chapter
FSL Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc.
description: Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated is an organization of college educated women committed to the constructive development of its members and to public service with a primary focus on the Black community.

name: FSL Gamma Zeta Alpha Fraternity, Inc.
description: The mission of Gamma Zeta Alpha Fraternity, Inc., a not-for-profit corporation built on the foundation of respect and brotherhood, is to establish and promote a nurturing environment at the university level and beyond, through Academic Excellence, Community Service, and the Celebration of the Diverse Latino Culture.

name: FSL Interfraternity Council
description: The mission of the Interfraternity Council at Stanford University is to promote and perpetuate the best interests of its member fraternities and the University, foster community among all Greek organizations, and cultivate cooperative relationships among all member organizations, university administration, and the community.

name: FSL Intersorority Council
description: The Stanford Inter-Sorority Council values inclusivity, diversity, intellectual vitality, and deep friendship. The members in Stanford Greek life dedicate themselves to philanthropic service and hope to serve their college community both within and outside of the Greek system. By engaging with the institutions upon which our organizations were built, we strive to make positive change by serving as leaders in our communities and redefining what it means to be a member in Greek life.

name: FSL Kappa Alpha
description: Our mission is to equip our members with a deep sense of community stewardship, an understanding of the value of diversity, the experience necessary to accelerate their role as impactful leaders, and a trusted network that allows them to take bold leaps into the opportunity of their life.

name: FSL Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity Incorporated
description: Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc. (ΚΑΨ) is a collegiate Greek-letter fraternity, founded on January 5, 1911 at Indiana University Bloomington. It is the 2nd oldest existing collegiate historically Black Greek letter fraternity and the 1st intercollegiate fraternity incorporated as a national body.The fraternity has over 250,000 members with 700 undergraduate and alumni chapters in every state of the United States, and international chapters in the United Kingdom, Germany, Korea, Japan, the Caribbean, Saint Thomas, Saint Croix, U.S. Virgin Islands, Nigeria, Bermuda, Canada, Dubai, Dominican Rep

name: FSL Kappa Alpha Theta
description: Our mission is to offer women-identifying people lifelong opportunities for intellectual, moral, and personal growth.

name: FSL Kappa Kappa Gamma
description: The purpose of this Chapter shall be: To unite members in a close bond of friendship and provide members with a supportive and empowering community. To properly maintain the organization and operation of the chapter, and to shift the role of the chapter as times change so as to continue to serve its members and the campus community. To cooperate with the host institution in advancing academic interests. To cooperate with other campus organizations in solving mutual problems and building higher standards of community involvement and responsibility. To develop an organization that is both accept

name: FSL Kappa Sigma
description: Kappa Sigma Fraternity is focused on the Four Pillars of Fellowship, Leadership, Scholarship and Service. Our chapter (Beta-Zeta) is committed to these values and our members interact with the larger community in accordance with them. Our members are heavily involved in the Stanford campus, in groups that include sports (both at the varsity and club levels), Mock Trial, Stanford Daily, Robber Barons, Stanford Consulting, and many more. name: FSL Lambda Phi Epsilon
description: To guide men on a lifelong discovery of authenticity and personal growth.

name: FSL Lambda Theta Nu Sorority, Inc.
description: Our mission is to promote and foster Latina leaders through educational and professional development, relationship building and community involvement. Our intent is to provide our members exposure to resources for continued growth.

name: FSL Omega Psi Phi Fraternity, Inc.
description: Since its humble beginnings as the first fraternity to be founded at an HBCU, the Omega Psi Phi Fraternity, Inc. continues to be on the front line, leveraging over one hundred years of its power, influence, and commitment to the uplift of our people, our communities, and our country. The fraternity motto is "Friendship is Essential to the Soul" and the cardinal principles are Manhood, Scholarship, Perseverance, and Uplift.

name: FSL Phi Kappa Psi Fraternity
description: The Phi Kappa Psi Fraternity engages men of integrity, further develops their intellect and enhances community involvement. With a legacy built on acceptance and trust, each brother realizes his highest potential through a lifelong experience of service and excellence.

name: FSL Pi Beta Phi
description: To promote friendship, develop people of intellect and integrity, cultivate leadership potential and enrich lives through community service.

name: FSL Sigma Alpha Epsilon
description: Membership in Sigma Alpha Epsilon requires fairness and respect toward all human beings, honesty and calmness in the face of adversity, and above all else, humility. We, as brothers of Sigma Alpha Epsilon, choose to adhere to these values and to do everything in our power to act as a force for good amongst ourselves and throughout Stanford University. We understand that being a member of this brotherhood is a privilege, and we vow to challenge our brothers toward maximizing the opportunity we have been given. Men who are and will be initiated into Sigma Alpha Epsilon voluntarily accept members

name: FSL Sigma Chi
description: While Sigma Chi's core values are Friendship, Justice and Learning, our vision is to be the preeminent leadership and character development brotherhood benefitting our members throughout life. Our mission is to develop values-based leaders committed to the betterment of character, campus and community. In the pursuit of these high ideals, the Sigma Chi Fraternity is able to offer tremendous value in augmenting the collegiate experience and supporting the lifelong journey of each of its members. We hope to assist brothers in becoming men of character, caring husbands, compassionate fathers and

name: FSL Sigma Nu Fraternity, Beta Chi Chapter
description: To allow communities to thrive.

name: FSL Sigma Phi Epsilon
description: Stanford SigEp's mission is to advance our community values of inclusion, community welfare, and academic and social enrichment. These values guide the totality of our actions from our individual lives to our member interactions to our community engagement and beyond. Inclusion Community for all. We aim to build and foster a Stanford community actively and intentionally inclusive to all people based on mutual understanding, compassion, and empathy. name: Furries at Stanford
description: Our purpose is to serve the interests of furries (fans of anthropomorphic animals) in the Stanford community through education on topics related to, and community building centered around, the furry fandom.

name: Future Advancers of Science and Technology
description: This organization is founded on the collective interest between graduate students, high school students, and high school faculty to engage and empower the next generation of scientists, especially students who belong to groups that are underrepresented in STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) professions. Graduate student mentors will lead and work alongside teams of high school students to answer open questions in science or conduct novel engineering studies inspired by students' curiosities. name: Gay Jesus Group
description: We are a grace-filled, Christ-centered community, welcoming ALL Stanford students: Lutherans, Episcopalians, Presbyterians, Methodists, Baptists, Catholics, people of any or no faith, seekers, skeptics, devotees, sinners, saints, LGBTQ2SIA+ folks, cisgender and straight folks, poets, scientists – everyone. Bring your doubts, your hopes, your questions, your longing for community and authenticity, your search for worship and connection. name: Global Health Student Council
description: The Undergraduate Global Health Club (UGHC) has three core missions: 1) to foster community among faculty, staff, and students interested in global health, 2) to facilitate interdisciplinary learning about global health, and 3) to connect students to the Center for Innovation in Global Health (CIGH) and non-CIGH opportunities in global health.

name: GradQ
description: An educational, social, and community-focused group for current Stanford graduate and professional students who hold queer identities, including but not limited to lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, asexual, and questioning, as well as allies of queer communities.

name: Graduate Catholic Student Association
description: The Graduate Catholic Student Association is a family of graduate students. Through a variety of social, educational, liturgical, and community service programs, we seek to form the Christian conscience, help members appropriate the Catholic faith, educate for justice, facilitate personal development, and form leaders for the future. We support the University's efforts to achieve its goals in keeping with our own traditions and in an environment of religious and cultural diversity.

name: Graduate Mathematics Outreach Organization
description: The primary activities of the SGMOO are the Directed Reading Program (DRP) and Stanford Women in Math Mentoring program (SWIMM). In the DRP, graduate students ("mentors") are matched with interested undergraduate students ("mentees") to read a mathematical text over the course of a quarter. SWIMM is a mentoring program that aims to reduce the gender gap in mathematics, in which undergraduates interested in math and computational science are paired with graduate student mentors from math, statistics, and ICME.

name: Graduate Music Studies Forum
description: The Graduate Music Studies Forum (GMSF) serves to centralize, facilitate, and efficiently coordinate ongoing projects, professional development events, and music departmental responsibilities that concern students involved in the academic study of music and sound.

name: Graduate Students in Electrical Engineering
description: GSEE is the graduate student group of the Electrical Engineering department at Stanford University. Founded in January 2011, GSEE aims to improve student life, strengthen relations between students, and foster communication with faculty and administration. Our mission is to create an atmosphere of support as well as leverage resources for the academic and personal development of graduate students within the department.

name: Graduate Students of Applied Physics and Physics
description: The Graduate Students of Applied Physics and Physics is an organization that is associated with the graduate students in the Physics Department and the Applied Physics Department at Stanford University. Our mission is to improve student life, support interactions among graduate students in different research groups, contribute to the personal and professional development of graduate students, and improve communication with faculty and administration in these departments.

name: GSB Adam Smith Society
description: The Adam Smith Society seeks to stimulate and promote discussion and debate of free-market economics and policies with the Stanford Graduate School of Business community and the broader Stanford community through large speaker events, smaller dinners and lunches with guests, and social events.

name: GSB Aerospace and Defense Club
description: The Club’s mission is to foster a GSB aviation, aerospace and defense technology community that develops future industry leaders and entrepreneurs by providing students opportunities to interact with established alumni founders/executives, company tours, and industry networking.

name: GSB Africa Business Club
description: The Africa Business Club at Stanford GSB exists to foster a vibrant, inclusive community of students passionate about Africa. We hope to create platforms for dialogue, connection, and action by: - Facilitating authentic conversations about African business, policy, innovation, and culture - Showcasing African changemakers and trailblazers through speaker series and events - Connecting students with leaders and changemakers on the continent - Building a bridge between Stanford GSB and Africa through collaboration, career exploration, and community Our aim is to spark curiosity, deepen understan

name: GSB Artificial Intelligence Club
description: The purpose of the Stanford GSB Artificial Intelligence (AI) Club is to serve GSB students, faculty members, and the broad Stanford community as the bridge between frontier development in AI and its applications and influence on the business and social worlds. To achieve that, AI Club is Stanford's central hub for: - Dialogue on business and social applications of AI - Connecting Club members with AI industry leaders - Receiving and accumulating the most holistic and up-to-date information about professional, business, and learning opportunities on AI at Stanford and beyond. By doing this, the

name: GSB Arts, Media & Entertainment Club
description: We strive to increase awareness, knowledge, and opportunity at the GSB in the arts, media, and entertainment (AME) arenas, including film, TV, music, publishing, and new media technology. Our goals are 1) to educate members about the fundamentals and future of these industries; 2) increase professional opportunities for students; 3) promote network-building with alumni and industry representatives, and 4) showcase the creative talent and artistic diversity within the GSB community. The AME Club is made up of over 140 active MBAs as well as other graduate students, including Knight Fellows and

name: GSB Asian Business Student Association
description: 1. Create a supportive community for Asian students navigating life at the GSB. Through welcome events, retreats, and small group gatherings, ABSA aims to build deep, lasting bonds among its members that extend far beyond the classroom. We foster a space where members find a sense of belonging and feel supported to thrive at the GSB. 2. Celebrate and share the richness of Asian cultures with the broader GSB community. We believe every Asian student should feel proud of where they come from and have the opportunity to share their unique cultural identities and experiences. Through various cultu

name: GSB Atelier
description: GSB Atelier exists to make formal, technique-based visual arts education accessible to the Stanford GSB community through structured instruction, guided studio practice, and constructive critique in a supportive, non commercial setting. We welcome students of all experience levels and focus on building foundational skills in drawing and painting, including observation, composition, value, color, perspective, and anatomy. By creating a consistent space for making art alongside peers, we aim to strengthen creative confidence, attention, and reflection, and to contribute to a more balanced and co

name: GSB Australia and New Zealand Club
description: The purpose of the Australia and New Zealand Club is to represent the interests of Australian, New Zealand, and Oceania-based Stanford students or students interested in living, working in, or visiting the regions. Specifically, we aim to provide a platform for professional development and networking opportunities, and for students to learn more about the Oceania region.

name: GSB Basketball Club
description: The Basketball Club aims to enrich the student community at the GSB by creating a positive basketball community—composed of a diverse group of students within the GSB. In pursuit of these goals, the Basketball Club actively seeks to appeal to a broad range of GSB students; promote and coordinate basketball activities within the GSB including intramurals, tournaments, and ongoing basketball activities within the GSB.

name: GSB Black Business Student Association
description: The Black Business Student Association (BBSA) serves as a support network for Black MBA, MSx, and PhD students at the Stanford Graduate School of Business (GSB). It also strives to enhance the GSB experience for all students; membership is open to all GSB students interested in cultural and professional issues that affect African-Americans. The BBSA provides the opportunity for students to serve as mentors to local high school and undergraduate students, and interact with African-American GSB alumni. The annual gala presents a forum for the community to come together and discuss relevant issue

name: GSB Business & Environment Club
description: The Business & Environment Club's goal is to cultivate a GSB community that incorporates environmental sustainability into its philosophy, curriculum, and operations. It also empowers its students and alumni to lead on environmental challenges in their industries. We focus on the following three themes through our activities: 1) Foster collaborations and robust discussions about sustainability at the GSB by leveraging the passion and connections of all members of the Stanford community; 2) Serve as a guidepost and all-encompassing resource at the intersection of business and the environment fo

name: GSB Canada Club
description: Our purpose is to foster a community for all students interested in learning, working, and connecting with Canada. Our mission is three-fold: 1) Learn: Hear from Canadian business leaders and classmates on how they have navigated and led their careers both within and outside of Canada 2) Work: Create opportunities for students to source meaningful internship and full-time opportunities in Canada 3) Connect: Build community between GSB students and the broader Bay Area Canadian community

name: GSB Catholic Student Association
description: The GSB Catholic Student Association (CSA) is committed to fostering a spiritual element within the GSB. We coordinate religious and social interaction amongst GSB Catholics, extending from weekly mass and prayer sessions, to BBQs, talks and other social events. All Catholics, practicing and otherwise, as well as other GSBers of common values, are encouraged to sign up and participate. The GSB CSA aims to play a visible and productive role within the broader and highly active Stanford Catholic Community.

name: GSB Christians in Business
description: Christians in Business provides an opportunity to develop lasting relationships within the GSB as we discuss and debate everyday life issues from a Christian perspective. We provide fellowship and numerous social events to build a supportive community within the GSB and in the marketplace beyond business school. The club is very active. We have weekly meetings, as well as alumni dinners, parties, and other social events.

name: GSB Coffee Club
description: The GSB Coffee Club exists to foster community, connection, and a shared passion for coffee among Stanford GSB students. Through gatherings, education, and engagement with the broader coffee ecosystem, the club provides a daytime, non-alcoholic space for students to build meaningful relationships over the world’s second most traded commodity.

name: GSB Consumer & Retail Club
description: The Consumer & Retail Club is designed for students interested in learning about or pursuing a career in the consumer & retail industry, both from an operating and investing perspective. Events throughout the year promote learning across the consumer industry and multiple retail sales channels (brick and mortar, direct-to-consumer, eCommerce, etc). In addition, events are organized to expose members to companies in a variety of segments and functional areas within the industry.
