name: GSB Dance Club
description: Make dance across cultures accessible regardless of technical experience, background, or financial status: - Create a space for classmates to learn new styles (including hip hop, contemporary, lyrical, ballroom, Bollywood, Bhangra, Salsa, AfroBeats, K-Pop, line dancing) by holding regular beginner classes from dance styles around the world - Run mini performances/flash mobs in celebration of different cultural days or festivities e.g. Diwali, Christmas, independence days, Africa Day etc. - Offer dance as an exercise-alternative for those looking for new ways to move, stay fit, and get a mental

name: GSB Disability & Caregiving Community
description: Our purpose is to cultivate a disability-oriented community at the GSB that is inclusive, accessible, and well-educated / informed. This club will be composed of students with disabilities and caregivers (all self-disclosed), and will conduct initiatives targeting three stakeholder groups.

name: GSB Education Club
description: Education tops many political and social agendas today, and there has been a growing interest in the private sector in the business of education. The Education Club engages Stanford business and education school students in discussions about education issues, their role in education, and business' role in education. The Education Club focuses on four broad areas: Building community and increasing knowledge among GSB and Ed students interested in education Assisting GSB students with the exploration of education careers Providing practical information for MBA/ MA Education dual-degree candidate

name: GSB Energy Club
description: The GSB Energy Club's mission is to enable students from all backgrounds to pursue their interests in energy, from oil and gas, smart grid, transportation, renewables, finance, and security to sustainability. Our goal is to foster an "energy-dense" community of students, faculty, alumnae, and industry professionals who will lead our world through the next global energy transition. Club activities include: Student support on classes and opportunities at Stanford Silicon Valley Career treks Alumnae networking nights Small group dinners with faculty and industry professionals On-campus lunches wi

name: GSB Entrepreneur Club
description: The Entrepreneur Club is for people with a strong interest in the practical aspects of entrepreneurship. Some Entrepreneur Club members have already owned a company, others are exploring potential business ideas, and others are just playing with an idea to pivot into entrepreneurship. We have events for everyone, just be curious! Our goals are: - To equip out members with knowledge, inspiration, network, and information to jump-start their entrepreneurial urges - To supplement the strong entrepreneurial curriculum at the GSB with exposure to, mentorship, and networking opportunities with outsi

name: GSB Europe Club
description: The Europe Club is a community gathering all students sharing an interest in European culture and business. Our goal is to provide a space for European students to share their culture and non-European students to discover it through the organization of social and cultural events (e.g. European movie nights, small group dinners, wine & cheese nights, parties). We also want to help GSB students explore European career opportunities via the organization of BBLs with European employers and networking events with European alumni.

name: GSB Family Business Club
description: The Stanford GSB Family Business Club is a home for those who want to build enduring, sustainable enterprises that often fall outside of the traditional Silicon Valley VC-fueled growth. We exist to empower GSB students who are committed to creating or scaling lasting and impactful businesses that transcend generations. Our mission is to provide a collaborative space for learning and growth as we explore the unique opportunities and challenges of long-term institutions such as family-owned businesses. The business model of such institutions often differs from that of startups or large corporati

name: GSB FemHealth Club
description: Inspire innovation in women's health and wellness through an interdisciplinary community of members passionate about building a more equitable world.

name: GSB Finance & Investment Club
description: The Finance & Investment Club is dedicated to the development of investment skills and financial industry knowledge among GSB students. Events include treks, BBLs, company presentations, social events, and investment idea pitches. The club also manages a real portfolio as part of the Stanford GSB endowment.

name: GSB FinTech Club
description: The FinTech Club is designed for students interested in learning about or pursuing a career in the financial technology industry. The club seeks to bring together students, faculty, entrepreneurs, company builders, and investors around a shared interest in the business and societal impact of financial technology. Events throughout the year promote community across all FinTech sub-verticals: banking, credit, insurtech, payments, asset/wealth management, and software.

name: GSB First Generation and/or Low Income Club
description: FGLI aims to create a community among students who are first-generation low-income, helping them find each other and facilitating more meaningful connections through shared experiences. GSB FLI also aims to develop programming with a far-reaching impact on business and education access for low-income students and young professionals. We aim to bring together FLI and non-FLI business school students to engage in discussions around class and socioeconomic topics to create more potent and effective FLI supporters among the future business leaders at the GSB.

name: GSB Food & Agribusiness Club
description: GSB Food & Agriculture Club serves to facilitate food and agriculture-related dialogue for the purposes of educational, professional, social, and entrepreneurial pursuits.

name: GSB Friends of TALK
description: Friends of TALK functions as the steward organization for TALK, a hallmark tradition of the Stanford GSB experience in which students share their life stories with classmates in a vulnerable, intimate, and supportive setting. TALK exists to support Stanford GSB students in the process of self-reflection and meaning-making of their lives; to encourage an appreciation and empathy for the vast diversity of experiences represented within the Stanford GSB student body; and to strengthen community and facilitate relationship-building within and between the two MBA classes at Stanford GSB. To that en

name: GSB Future of Cities
description: The purpose of the GSB Future of Cities Club is to provide an intersection point for cross-industry and cross-sectoral dialogue around complex issues and potential solutions that arise from urbanization. We will explore ways to make cities more livable, equitable, and sustainable through urban innovations, the transformation of traditional industries, governmental policies, and the participation of civil society.

name: GSB Future Of Mobility Club
description: The purpose of the FOM club is to help GSB students gain a deeper understanding of the rapidly changing mobility landscape that is being disrupted by self-driving and flying cars, new ownership models, and multi-modal transport models. These changes will have an unprecedented effect on hundreds of thousands of jobs in the US economy - and on society as a whole - and at the same time, create new business opportunities for entrepreneurs. We will explore the four big trends that are actively challenging the existing infrastructure: Connectivity: Cars will be able to communicate with each other, t

name: GSB Gaming Club
description: The purpose of the Gaming Club is to provide an environment for people to explore the gaming industry. The club focuses on two goals -- one on the business side and one on the social side. On the business side, the club provides a place to gain insights into the industry and help students develop new venture ideas. On the social side, the club provides opportunities to network with other people interested in the gaming industry both within and outside the GSB, Stanford, and the Bay Area.

name: GSB Golf Club
description: The GSB Golf Club's mission is to provide its members with opportunities to learn one of the most critical and underappreciated business skills, the game of golf. To help members improve their level of play, the club will organize various playing opportunities including: instructional clinics focusing on all aspects of the game, tournament-style competitions at various golf courses in the northern California area, and casual group tee times at the Stanford Golf Course. Finally, the club will attempt to secure discounts on equipment from local retailers and lessons from local instructors.

name: GSB Government & Politics Club
description: The club's mission is to provide a non-partisan forum to discuss government and political issues, bring government officials to campus as speakers, and offer opportunities to meet with government officials in California and elsewhere. It also aims to support students with careers in the public sector and at the intersection of business and government, building a community that will last beyond the GSB.

name: GSB Greater China Business Club
description: The Greater China Business Club is a platform, interface, and exchange for people interested in business in the Greater China region: Mainland China, Taiwan, Hong Kong. The club will provide opportunities to connect, share knowledge, learn, discover, and create opportunities. First and foremost, we strive to improve our members' ability to succeed in Greater China-related business. We seek to do this by: (i) Pooling and expanding our networks with GSB and Stanford alumni as well as other members of the Greater China business community; (ii) Conducting educational events to increase the depth o

name: GSB Health & Wellbeing Club
description: The purpose of the club is to help the GSB community with well-being assistance and interventions such as nutrition counseling, Graham Weaver sessions, workout classes, and meditation workshops. This expanded focus can also help bring wellness-focused speakers, companies, and researchers to the GSB. The club also provides mental health industry-focused events and programming at GSB, including, but not limited to, info sessions, BBLs, recruiting, partnerships, etc. Finally, the club supports GSB students who are interested in wellness and/or mental health-related careers.

name: GSB Healthcare Club
description: The Stanford Healthcare Club is the primary life science and health care industry-oriented student organization at Stanford. We are headquartered at the Graduate School of Business, but our membership is interdisciplinary and drawn from the breadth of Stanford's graduate schools, including MBA, MD, JD, and Ph.D./postdoctoral programs. Our mission is to build networks that will help Stanford students explore, pursue and continue careers in businesses related to health care and the life sciences, including biotechnology & genomics, health care, pharmaceuticals, health care information technology

name: GSB Hispanic Business Student Association
description: Our vision for HBSA is to create an inclusive community that: 1) Celebrates Hispanic/Latine heritage, 2) Provides a community and safety net for Hispanic/Latine classmates, 3) Fosters connections between the GSB, alumni, and organizations that promote advancement of Hispanic/Latine leadership, and 4) Supports members in navigating and thriving at the GSB. HBSA is a community of leaders and proponents of Hispanic/Latine people and their personal and professional development at the GSB, in the broader community, and across all types of organizations. We invite classmates who identify as Hispanic

name: GSB Improvisational Theater Troupe
description: We are a GSB-specific organization open to the entire Stanford community. Our mission is to provide access to the art of improvisational acting, and through improvisational acting to help students and staff gain comfort in public speaking and experiential role playing. For our performers, we aim to create a welcoming environment for personal risk-taking and development and for our audience, a sense of community and many belly laughs.

name: GSB Jewish Business Student Association
description: The mission of the Jewish Business Student Association is to provide a welcoming Jewish community for all GSB students and their significant others. Through the JBSA, we are building a community that allows us to keep in touch, celebrate our high-holidays, and make new friends. The Club organizes the traditional festivities around Jewish high-holidays and sponsors other educational, social and religious events to enrich the cultural life of the GSB community. JBSA intends to reach across and bridge over the diversity of Jewish practices, backgrounds, and interests to strengthen the relationshi

name: GSB Latin American Student Association
description: The Latin American Student Association (LASA) has the goal of strengthening the bonds among the Latin community at the GSB and all those interested in it while at the same time increasing the awareness of the GSB community in Latin issues. To fulfill its end, LASA organizes not only parties, barbecues, and other social gatherings but also speakers series, career development activities, and academic-related events.

name: GSB Latter-day Saint Student Association
description: The GSB Latter-day Saint Association is a socially and spiritually enriching community of Latter-day Saint students. We gather regularly to discuss gospel-related topics, learn from Latter-day Saint business and spiritual leaders, and build relationships. We encourage latter-day saints to participate, regardless of church involvement, and we warmly welcome all students interested in contributing to an uplifting community.

name: GSB Management Consulting Club
description: The Consulting Club serves members of the GSB community who have an interest or background in the management consulting industry. We focus on helping current GSB students explore careers in consulting and prepare for the rigorous case interview process

name: GSB Manufacturing & Supply Chain Club
description: The Manufacturing & Supply Chain Club brings together students interested in how things are made, moved, and scaled in the real economy. In an era defined by technological change, geopolitical complexity, and sustainability challenges, the physical economy is more critical than ever. The club equips students with the insights, networks, and real-world exposure needed to build, scale, acquire, and transform businesses rooted in this space. We do so through workshops, treks, small-group dinners, and conversations with industry leaders and fellow members.

name: GSB MBA Student Association
description: The MBA students of the Stanford Graduate School of Business hereby establish a Student Association to represent themselves and to act on their collective behalf in order to actively enrich and broaden the experience of the student community, both inside and outside of the classroom. In pursuit of these goals, the SA will represent, advocate, and act on student views and concerns; promote, coordinate, and operate student activities and services; and enhance channels of communication between the student, faculty, administration, alumni and university communities.

name: GSB Middle East and North Africa Club
description: The Middle East and North Africa club promotes: The Middle East and North Africa within the GSB through speakers and recruiting events and conferences. The GSB within the Middle East and North Africa through admission and alumni events. The club's focus is strictly on promoting the business and cultural aspects of the region, leaving the political part to other clubs at Stanford that are better suited.

name: GSB Midwest Club
description: The Midwest Club aims to foster cultural awareness, build community, and celebrate all things relating to the Midwest at the GSB.

name: GSB MSx Student Association
description: The Stanford MSx students of the Stanford Graduate School of Business hereby establish a Student Association to represent themselves and to act on their collective behalf in order to actively enrich and broaden the experience of die student community, both inside and outside of the classroom.

name: GSB Outdoors Club
description: go outside

name: GSB PhD Association
description: The PhD Student Association works to enrich the quality of social and academic life for doctoral students in Stanford's Graduate School of Business.

name: GSB Pickleball Club
description: The Stanford GSB Pickleball Club aims to foster a vibrant and inclusive community that promotes physical well-being and social connectivity among students at the Graduate School of Business. Our mission is to provide a platform where members can engage in the exciting sport of pickleball, regardless of skill level, creating an environment that encourages camaraderie, healthy competition, and lifelong connections.

name: GSB Pride
description: Pride Club is a social and socially active organization for gay, lesbian, bisexual, transgender, queer, and questioning students and allies at Stanford GSB. The goals are to provide a community for LGBTQ students and allies; to serve as a resource for our membership and the Stanford GSB Community as a whole; and to increase awareness of LGBTQ issues in business. Activities include social gatherings on campus and throughout the Bay Area, educational and awareness-building events, participation in the LGBTQ MBA Conference, and networking events with gay and lesbian alumni and with complementary

name: GSB Private Equity Club
description: The Private Equity Club is devoted to fostering awareness of and interest in the private investment industry throughout the GSB community. Our activities focus on middle-stage growth equity and late-stage LBO investment activities. We encourage students with and without industry experience to participate. This year, we plan on hosting leading principals, headhunters, and advisors who can offer a variety of perspectives on current topics of interest within the private equity industry. These speakers will act as a conduit to the GSB's vast network of "buy-side" alumni. Other planned activities i

name: GSB Product Club
description: The Product Club focuses on all things product! Whether you're building your own product, want to help a company successfully develop and launch better products, or are interested in connecting with people over product - Product Club is for you! We host social, professional, and skill-building events, showcase internship and job opportunities, and connect you with peers, alums, and industry professionals in product!

name: GSB Real Estate Club
description: The Real Estate Club focuses on the buildings, spaces, and communities where people live, work, and play. Finance, economics, legal and regulatory procedures, prop tech, architecture and design, and urban planning are topics that may be covered in this forum.

name: GSB Run Club
description: Stanford GSB Run Club is an inclusive, contagiously fun running community that brings people together through movement

name: GSB Search Fund Club
description: The Search Fund Club's mission is to provide an introduction to entrepreneurship through acquisition for students exploring the industry, as well as a platform to accelerate the launch of a formal search fund for students who have already committed to the career path.

name: GSB Show
description: Every year, near the middle of spring quarter, the entire GSB community awaits with bated breath the most spectacular--nay, only--quasi-artistic performance to be put on by the business school. The annual GSB show is a long-standing tradition here at Stanford. It is entirely student-written and student-run, and consists of videos, skits, and hilarious song and dance numbers, all designed to bring a bit of humor (that's humour for the Europeans among us) and wit to an institution that, uhm, can use it! Use the GSB Show as a forum to exact your own personal revenge on, or to celebrate, your D&D

name: GSB Soccer Club
description: The GSB Soccer Club aims to promote a balance between fun and serious soccer for all GSB students who are interested in the world's greatest sport. We welcome all levels of skill and involvement. For those who love playing, we plan a number of big events throughout the year, including the UCLA Tournament, Austin Tournament, California Cup, and MBA1s vs. MBA2s. Additionally, we have pick-up games 1-2 times a week throughout the year that are open to everyone. We look forward to seeing you out there!

name: GSB Social Impact Club
description: The Social Impact Club serves Stanford GSB students interested in exploring innovative ways to tackle the world's most pressing social challenges and improving livelihoods for those in need, both in the US and worldwide. The club aims to explore how innovation across business, finance, policy, and nonprofit systems can better catalyze long-term social impact.

name: GSB South Asian Business Students Association
description: SABSA's purpose is to create social community and affinity networks through shared experiences & activities for South Asian students and those interested in South Asian culture at GSB.

name: GSB Sports Management Club
description: Whether you are a die-hard sports fan or a sports industry veteran looking to deepen your network, the Sports Management Club is a perfect fit for you. The Sports Management Club hosts guest speakers, plans small group dinners, sets up career panels, and organizes outings with those involved in the business side of sports and related industries. Recent examples include general managers and presidents of sports organizations (e.g., Sam Hinkie -- GM of the Philadelphia 76ers; Dave Kaval -- President of the Oakland Athletics), league executives (e.g., Amy Brooks -- President of Team Marketing & B

name: GSB Tech Club
description: Located in the heart of Silicon Valley, the Stanford Graduate School of Business is geographically and strategically positioned to take advantage of a wealth of technology companies headquartered and thriving within its vicinity. The Tech Club is open to members of the Stanford GSB community with a passion for technologies ranging from consumer to enterprise, software to hardware, mobile to wearable. The mission of Tech Club is to empower its members to explore the technology industry, regardless of their background. There are several dimensions in which the Tech Club operates and advances Sta

name: GSB Texas Club
description: The Texas Club is comprised of students who are from Texas, who are interested in finding jobs in Texas, or who simply have an interest in Texan issues! Our mission is to foster a Texas community at the GSB that builds relationships (through monthly social events such as barbecues and game watching parties), facilitates professional development (through career treks and BBLs with industry leaders and Texas-based companies), and fosters Texas pride (by hosting cultural events such as a trek to the Houston Livestock Show & Rodeo).

name: GSB The Tea Table
description: Tea is a communal activity that spans cultures and countries. We bring together experienced enthusiasts and those with budding interest to learn and try teas from across the world. While tea is our medium, our purpose is to offer students a quiet, welcoming ritual through which they can pause, recharge, and connect in a more human and unforced way.

name: GSB Travel and Hospitality Club
description: The Travel & Hospitality (T&H) club seeks to become the center for travel and hospitality-related interactions at the GSB. We aim to bring together students, faculty and guests to explore issues related to all aspects of leisure and business travel including hotels and resorts, restaurants, the airline and car rental industries, vacation real estate, eco-tourism, spa/golf/adventure, sport-related travel, etc. The T&H leadership aims to focus on the following areas: (i) Careers & Professional Development, (ii) Networking, and (iii) Social Events.

name: GSB Venture Capital Club
description: The Venture Capital Club is one of the largest and most popular student organizations at the Stanford Graduate School of Business. The club sponsors a variety of group events with venture capitalists and entrepreneurs, including small group dinners, speaker presentations, workshops, and social events. Club members range from those with previous VC experience to those who are exploring the venture industry for the first time. The Venture Capital Club's mission is to facilitate: Education - Help club members learn about the venture capital industry and the fundraising and investment process thro

name: GSB Veterans Club
description: The Veterans Club is the GSB's association of military veterans. While all ex-military MBA and MSx students are automatically members, the club is open to all GSB students and attempts to relate the unique experiences of military service to current events and business problems that managers are likely to encounter, including strategic, human resources, and operational issues. The Veterans Club also provides an opportunity to help MBA1 club members who are seeking a private-sector position for the first time with advice concerning the recruiting process, including writing resumes, industry and

name: GSB Volleyball Club
description: The GSB Volleyball Club aims to foster an inclusive community for volleyball that promotes physical health and social connectivity among students at the Graduate School of Business. Our mission is to provide a space for people of all levels to come learn, compete and play volleyball across campus. We want to build lifelong connections and encourage teamwork amongst all.

name: GSB Wine Circle
description: The GSB Wine Circle seeks to provide a foundation of knowledge and tasting experiences to further students' enjoyment and understanding of wine. The Wine Circle offers opportunities to develop closer relationships between students, faculty, and industry insiders in an informal social setting. This year there will be four focuses to the Wine Circle's events: Accessible Wine - Events for those of you who want exposure to a variety of wines. Each of these events will focus on one aspect of wine. Educational Events - A series of educational events catered for those who know nothing about wine to t

name: GSB Women in Management
description: Women in Management (WIM) is a strong, authentic community of members who aim to build a supportive network and foster a more equitable and gender-mindful business world by: Building an inclusive and supportive community of women and men from diverse backgrounds who inspire each other to develop personally and professionally. Helping all members of the GSB community become gender-mindful leaders who are aware of the challenges facing women at work and prepared to advocate for a level playing field for all. Building strong professional networks that empower Stanford women in the workplace and s

name: Habla
description: Habla is a community-engaged learning organization in which students coach English as a Second Language (ESL) to native Spanish-speaking workers on campus. We match Stanford students with custodians, landscapers, dining hall workers, and other staff members for one-on-one language coaching. Habla focuses on real-world language skills, from handling parent-teacher conferences to studying for citizenship tests.

name: Healing Harmonies
description: Stanford Healing Harmonies is centered around the intersection of music, medicine, and service. We strive to promote healing through music by performing instrumental music off-campus at various community centers, providing opportunities for connection and engagement through music.

name: Healing Strokes
description: Healing Strokes hopes to facilitate relaxation-based art therapy for stroke patients and their carers with the goal of helping alleviate post-stroke depression often experienced during recovery. Post-stroke depression and related anxiety affects about a third of all stroke survivors, yet many hospitals often lack the proper mental wellness resources needed to address this issue. Under the guidance of neurologist Dr. Nirali Vora and occupational therapist Julie Muccini, we have crafted a relaxation-based art therapy curriculum using an integrated patient-carer team approach. By facilitating cre

name: Health EDU
description: We will bring together students on campus from a variety of backgrounds and disciplines who are passionate about health education, preventative care, and advocating for underserved youth. We aim to help Stanford students gain the critical teaching and facilitation skills necessary for careers in medicine, entrepreneurship, research, and more. We will provide direct opportunities for Stanford students to engage with the broader Bay community and gain experience in clinical settings. Opportunities include volunteering with schools, clinics, and LifeMoves shelters.

name: Health Education Lifetime Partnerships (HELP) for Kids
description: Our mission is to provide innovative and effective comprehensive health education to teens to prepare them for life's challenges. Our curriculum equips young middle schoolers with knowledge, skills, and tools to make sound choices and informed decisions for themselves.

name: Health Policy Collective
description: We hope to use the Health Policy Collective as a way to bridge the gap between healthcare delivery and policy behind decisions made by individuals, groups of physicians, hospitals, and the broader society. We believe by creating this group we will better understand how our political decisions shape healthcare and vice versa, and hopefully be more aware and engaged citizens ourselves.

name: Hellenic Association of Stanford
description: The Hellenic Association at Stanford aims to bring together people of Hellenic heritage and people who are interested in Hellenic culture, and engage them through cultural, social and recreational events.

name: Hermanas de Stanford
description: Hermanas is a social organization focused on supporting the academic, professional, personal, and community growth of Latine/x womxn and gender-marginalized folks at Stanford. We welcome all students who are interested to join!

name: Hindu Students Association
description: The Stanford Hindu Students Association was founded at Stanford with a threefold mission: 1. To foster an environment that brings together Hindus from all parts of the world who believe in the fundamental principles of love and respect of humanity and all that lives. 2. To lay claim to the ancient legacy of the sages that is open to all mankind, and study it with an open, scientific mind as the ancients have recommended. 3. To understand Hinduism in the modern context through the works and vision of Swami Vivekananda. Since its foundation, it's been a socially active and vibrant group doing mu

name: Hmong Student Union
description: Stanford Hmong Student Union (HSU) is the Hmong-interest student group at Stanford University that provides a supportive community for everyone interested! Our mission is to spread awareness of Hmong identity and presence at Stanford University as well as promote higher education among Hmong youth.

name: Hong Kong Student Association
description: To promote, encourage, and share Hong Kong culture, including Cantonese language and cultural traditions, on the Stanford campus.

name: Hopkins Marine Station Student Organization
description: The purpose of HMSSO is to increase community at the Hopkins Marine Station, bringing together undergraduate and graduate students from multiple departments. HMSSO will organize social and academic events of interest to the whole community, while addressing needs that are specific to the Hopkins Marine Station.-

name: Ideas Out Loud
description: The purpose of Ideas Out Loud, the student group that organizes TEDxStanford and various public speaking events, is to provide a platform for the Stanford community to share powerful stories and big ideas.

name: Improving Dreams, Equity, Access & Success
description: IDEAS aims to create a safe space and serve as a resource hub for the undocumented community at Stanford. We envision, and will work towards, building a student-led community focused on listening to and addressing the needs of undocumented students.

name: Indonesian Student Association at Stanford
description: The Indonesian Student Association at Stanford is a social and professional group of Indonesians, Indonesian-Americans, and students interested in Indonesian culture. Our mission is to spread awareness and appreciation of Indonesian cultural heritage while building and nurturing an inclusive and supportive community.

name: Innovative Styles
description: Innovative Styles' goal is to entertain and continue to turn the heads of the Stanford and Bay Area Communities with energetic, highly technical, contemporary dance and through new, cutting-edge student choreography. All Innovative Styles members strive to create an energetic performance outlet for a style of dance that was formerly unseen at Stanford University. In addition to participating as guest performers in cultural events, art events, halftime shows, and other groups' dance shows, Innovative Styles also organizes and performs in the Innovative Styles Spring Show every May. Innovative S

name: International Draftee Collective
description: The International Draftee Collective is committed to fostering a community of past, current, and future international draftees and draft-affiliated students at Stanford. The International Draftee Collective will help students navigate the national services of their respective countries by mentoring future Stanford conscripts about how to best approach their national duties and re-integrate veterans of international militaries returning from mandatory military service.

name: International Policy Students Association
description: The International Policy Students Association (IPSA) fosters community among graduate students within the Master's in International Policy (MIP) program and provides them with opportunities for personal and professional development. As the elected student government for MIP, it liaises with Freeman Spogli Institute (FSI) administration and faculty. IPSA is committed to racial equity, diversity, and inclusion and has officers dedicated to supporting these aims within MIP and FSI writ large.

name: InterVarsity Christian Fellowship
description: InterVarsity at Stanford is a multiethnic and interdenominational fellowship that is seeking Jesus together. Our community is all about Growing the Family of God: growing in relationship with God and one another as we invite more people to experience the love and good news of Jesus. Whether you have been a follower of Jesus for many years or are simply interested in exploring the Christian faith, you are welcome!

name: InterVarsity Graduate Christian Fellowship
description: InterVarsity Graduate Christian Fellowship (IVGrad) is a multi-ethnic and non-denominational community of graduate students who want to know Jesus Christ. We seek to grow spiritually, cultivate true Christian community, integrate faith and academic learning, and dedicate ourselves to witness and service. In particular, we encourage thought and discussion about what it means to be a Christian in an academic setting. We are not just a group “for Christians,” but also for those with little to no Christian background who wish to explore the Christian faith and experience the Christian community.

name: Jain Students Association
description: The Stanford Jain Students Association (Jain) is a VSO dedicated to bringing together students interested in learning about spirituality and inner connection, while providing a welcoming space to connect with Jain religion, culture, and values. Jain allows students to meet like-minded individuals and become part of a close-knit community where lifelong friendships are formed and supported. Together, this community organizes and celebrates events such as Paryushan and Mahavir Jayanti, plans trips to Jain temples and other universities, partners with on-campus organizations to lead large-scale c

name: Jewish Medical Student Association
description: We aspire to foster a space in which Jewish medical and PA students feel empowered to explore the facets of Judaism that matter most to them, including but not limited to religious observance, cultural discovery, and heritage exploration. Our primary goal is to host events that allow for students to bond and connect over their shared Jewish heritage, as well as to welcome all students and allies interested in learning more about Judaism.

name: Jewish Student Association
description: We're the Jewish Student Association, and our goal is simple: build a warm community where students can identify with Jewish culture and have a good time connecting with their peers. We strive to incorporate students across a wide spectrum of Jewish practice through programming that will appeal to all, including: religious ceremonies for holidays, weekly Shabbat celebrations, tikkun olam (social action/service), and social excursions such as special dinners and interfaith/intercultural events.

name: Kayumanggi
description: Kayumanggi, meaning "brown-skinned" in Tagalog, is the only Pilipinx cultural performance troupe at Stanford. We are open to dancers, singers, actors and actresses, and writers of all levels--no auditions required! Kayumanggi performs traditional Pilipinx folk dances that are as diverse as the many different islands in the Philippines. Kayu aims to promote awareness of Pilipinx culture through dance, art, music, and drama. We hope to create an outlet for self-exploration and discovery, encouraging inclusiveness and openness not just among Pilipinx-Americans, but with the greater Stanford and B

name: Keyboard Studies Committee
description: KSC serves as a close-knit community for keyboard students and acts as a liaison between keyboard students and the Stanford Music Department, involving members in planning and execution of keyboard-related initiatives, events, and projects.

name: Kids With Dreams
description: Kids With Dreams is a Stanford group that works with children and young adults in the Palo Alto area with intellectual and developmental disabilities. We organize a variety of weekly programming including basketball, volleyball, gymnastics, dance, karate, and life skills education. We also organize events within the quarter for the buddy program, like Silent Discos and Winter Formal. The aim of the program is to provide friendship and support for a variety of people in the community.

name: King International Development Association
description: KIDA exists to build an undergraduate community around international development at Stanford. KIDA pursues this purpose in collaboration with the King Center on Global Development while remaining a student-led organization governed by its members and officers.

name: Kol Etz A Capella
description: Kol Etz (the Voice of the Tree) is a Jewish a cappella group at Stanford dedicated to celebrating Jewish culture, community, and creativity through music. Rooted in tradition and reaching outward, we strive for musical excellence while reimagining Jewish expression through contemporary vocal performance. Through collaboration and song, we build an inclusive, welcoming community that honors the richness of Jewish heritage, amplifies diverse identities, and uses music as a bridge—connecting past and present, campus and community.

name: Korean Graduate Student Association
description: Our organization supports Korean students and alumni of various graduate school at Stanford University. Our internal work focuses on building a sense of community among the Korean graduate students and encouraging scholarly exchanges among them. Our external work includes hosting events and providing resources for students seeking to find employment at companies, universities or research centers.

name: Korean-American Student Association
description: KSA is a pan-ethnic, student-run undergraduate organization committed to fostering a welcoming community among students who identify as Korean or Korean American and/or share an interest in Korean culture, politics, and social issues.

name: Kurdish Association for Justice
description: The organization promotes awareness, discussion, and support of Kurdish and Kurdish-related issues. It also serves as a platform to showcase Kurdish culture and history, and give support to Kurdish students.

name: KZSU 90.1 FM
description: KZSU exists to provide radio broadcasting that serves the interests of the Stanford, Mid-Peninsula, and Bay Area communities. KZSU is proud to offer its services to the public. These services include, among other things, providing information and instructions during an emergency, producing innovative music programming, producing competent and informative news and sports programming, and broadcasting programs which are specifically dedicated to public service objectives. name: L'Chayim Club: Chabad at Stanford
description: We are a community center where Jews and non-jews alike can experience Judaism, its practices, food, and culture. Our mission is to provide a space whereby people can choose to learn more about Judaism, experience for themselves, and interact with fellow peers.

name: Latine Business Student Association
description: The Latine Business Student Association (LBSA) is a student-run, pre-professional organization at Stanford University. It strives to promote success through diversity, develop its members both personally and professionally, and create a Familia whose relationships continue beyond The Farm. As an organization, we leverage our capital to further Latine representation on campus and ensure that our members have access to the resources they need to thrive.

name: Latino Medical Student Association
description: The Stanford Chapter of the Latino Medical Student Association (LMSA) serves to advocate for the unique health needs and interests of the Hispanic and Latin American communities through education, outreach, and service. In addition, our chapter seeks to support Hispanic Latin American pre-medical students and medical trainees through mentorship and collaboration. Beyond Stanford, our chapter is one of twelve in the LMSA West region, and our members are active at the local, regional, and national level.

name: Latinos Unidos de Stanford
description: Latinos Unidos strives to equally represent and celebrate all Latin American cultures and ethnicities within the Stanford community. We focus and aim primarily to educate the Stanford community through social and cultural programming about the various Latin American celebrations, our rich history, literature, media productions, and diverse communities.

name: Latter-day Saint Student Association
description: The Latter-day Saint Student Association at Stanford is an organization centered upon creating and maintaining a strong community on campus for the members and friends of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Through our events, we strive to promote faith in Jesus Christ, support members of the LDSSA in their academic and personal lives, and uphold the standards of the LDS Church. Our events are open to all members of the Stanford community and we strive to provide opportunities for people to learn about our beliefs. name: Legacy Dance Team
description: Founded in 2016, Legacy Dance is Stanford's first and only competition choreography team. We strive for a culture of growth as dancers and strength as a community, and we welcome dancers from all backgrounds and levels of experience. Our dance draws from styles such as hip hop, house, contemporary, waacking, popping, and breaking among others. Our sets often have an emphasis on storytelling. Check us out on Instagram @lgcy_dance and on YouTube at https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCyZvl6HLc0NdBx2Ju4bqyrQ!

name: Leland Quarterly
description: Leland Quarterly: A Statement on Literature, Culture, Art, and Politics is the ink-and-paper home of Stanford art and writing. Our mission is to produce a quality arts and literature magazine that showcases the superlative talents of the Stanford community. We like to mix the fun with the scholarly, the abstract with the concrete, and we like to present all that in an attractive glossy magazine. LQ is made possible by funding from the ASSU Publications Board, The Stanford Fund, and the Stanford English Department, and by the impeccable work of Giant Horse Printing. name: Leland Stanford Junior University Marching Band
description: The LSJUMB seeks to provide a musical experience that is inclusive, accessible, and exciting for members new to their instruments as much as those who are more experienced. Members of the LSJUMB commit to a mindset of musical growth and community support, as well as to uphold the Band Norms and Values In performance, the LSJUMB is a scatter band, performing on the field, in rallies, and at campus and community events. The music of the LSJUMB is student-arranged and not restricted to any particular genre or subject to any external approval other than relevant and required licensing.

name: LGBTQ-Meds
description: We are dedicated to raising awareness of queer health issues and promoting equal social and political rights for lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender people. LGBTQ-Meds additionally functions as a support group, safe space, and social group for all graduate students and undergraduates regardless of sexual orientation who are interested in queer health issues.

name: Little Libraries
description: We are a Stanford student program that aims to spread the love for reading and literacy among young children, especially those in the waiting rooms of pediatric clinics in underserved communities. We read to children in these clinics, sterilize and clean books, and sort books to send to clinics and for kids to take home after their visit. We spread awareness on how to promote literacy at home and disseminate information to parents.

name: Los Hermanos de Stanford
description: Los Hermanos de Stanford stand as one, united, in exercising our beliefs: Active participation and collaboration with all communities, and servicing those less fortunate than ourselves who may find our assistance beneficial. A dedication to academic excellence, developing marketable skills and mental fortitude in preparation for life outside of the university; And the practice and preservation of our members' cultures, values, and ideals, never forgetting who we are and from where we have come We focuses on┬áfundraising for our annual┬áscholarship┬áwhich we award to┬áhigh achieving, low-income

name: Los Salseros de Stanford
description: Los Salseros de Stanford is Stanford University's only student group dedicated entirely to salsa! We perform, compete, and host salsa socials open to the Stanford community.

name: Love-All
description: Love-All is a student-run weekly athletic instruction program committed to inspiring a love for regular physical activity in individuals with intellectual developmental disabilities (IDDs). The club will offer a platform for Stanford students to share their love of athletic instruction to kids with IDD and offer professional training to develop the leadership, responsibility, and communication skills needed to teach children with IDDs.

name: Macao Student Association
description: The Macao Student Association (MSA) strives to promote, encourage and share Macao culture on the Stanford Campus.

name: Malaysians at Stanford
description: To provide an avenue and opportunity for Malaysians and those interested in Malaysian affairs (e.g., culture, politics, professional opportunities there) to meet, mingle, and discuss issues.

name: Mariachi Cardenal de Stanford
description: Our mission is to learn and perform Mariachi music so that members of the Stanford community can enjoy and also participate in the beauty of traditional Mexican music.

name: Marine Outreach for Learning and Advocacy in Students
description: Our project directly addresses the critical issue of unequal access to education in specialized fields like marine sciences, which are essential for fostering awareness and solutions for ocean sustainability. Subjects like marine sciences require specialized knowledge, tools, and expertise, often out of reach for students in marginalized schools. This inequity limits their understanding of ocean-related challenges and fuels a vicious cycle of limited opportunity, ultimately hindering efforts to build an ocean-literate society. name: Mechanical Engineering Women and Gender Minorities Group
description: The Mechanical Engineering Women and Gender Minorities Group is a group of graduate students committed to fostering a sense of community and environment among graduate women and gender minorities in engineering at Stanford University.

name: Med Students for Choice
description: The mission of the Stanford chapter of Medical Students for Choice (MSFC) is to equip medical students with the knowledge, skills, and values needed to provide compassionate, evidence-based, and justice-centered reproductive health care throughout their careers. As a medical-student–specific organization, MSFC uniquely focuses on clinical training, professional development, and career preparation—bridging the gap between reproductive justice principles and future practice. name: Medical Students with Disability and Chronic Illness
description: Medical Students with Disability and Chronic Illness (MSDCI) provides a support system and platform for advocacy for students with disabilities and chronic illness. We are also opening the conversation about the difficulties of becoming a healthcare provider while having personal experiences with illness and disease, and how these experiences can better inform our colleagues and patient care. We are committed to increasing resources and accessibility for MD and PA students living with disability/chronic illness at Stanford and in medicine as a whole. name: Medicine in Motion
description: Medicine in Motion strives to form a community among medical students and healthcare professionals in the setting of physical wellness, promoting camaraderie around recreational sports gatherings to ultimately combat physician burnout.

name: MedMentors at Stanford
description: MedMentors at Stanford is dedicated to expanding access to medical careers through structured, peer-led mentorship and practical guidance for undergraduate students navigating the path to medicine. Our mission is to provide free, near-peer mentorship from Stanford medical students to undergraduates exploring careers in medicine while helping navigate the medical school application process through workshops, advising, and shared resources. name: Mexican Association of Graduate Students at Stanford
description: The Mexican Association of Graduate Students at Stanford aims to: • Promote the knowledge of Mexican culture among the Stanford community; • Organize and support cultural, social, and recreational events for the Mexican students at Stanford and those interested in Mexico; • Provide information to prospective Mexican students; • Encourage the exchange of ideas about issues related to Mexico; • Provide a network for Mexican students at Stanford University

name: Middle Eastern and North African Students in Medicine
description: Our organization was created to foster an inclusive space for Middle Eastern and North African (MENA) students at the medical school. The main objective of MENAMeds is to develop a network of MENA-identifying health professionals at Stanford and to provide opportunities for MENA students and faculty to connect and organize in addressing important issues of medical representation. We hope to empower our members through mentorship, leadership, and advocacy.

name: MINT Magazine
description: Both a print publication and digital presence, MINT strives to highlight different trends sported by Stanford students and show off Stanford-originated art, style, and culture. We are a team of photographers, writers, designers, style enthusiasts, and artists who care deeply about creating a space for both creative expression and social good on campus.

name: Mixed Company
description: Stanford's oldest all-gender all-genre a cappella group.

name: Moment Christian Fellowship
description: To equip and unify Christians to communally cultivate, boldly share, and intellectually defend our faith, while helping seekers explore.

name: Mongolian Student Association at Stanford
description: The Mongolian Student Association at Stanford (MSAS) aims to become a thriving community, serving as a central hub for Mongolian students at Stanford and beyond. Our core purpose is to ignite and uplift Mongolian students and youth through various cultural and professional events. Whether you are a current student or a newcomer to our community, the Association is dedicated to making you feel welcome and supported on campus, thereby paving the way for your personal and professional growth.

name: Mua Lac Hong
description: Mua Lac Hong (MLH) is Stanford's only Vietnamese dance group. name: Music Enriching the Lives of Developing Youth
description: MELODY (Music Enriching the Lives of Developing Youth) is a volunteer organization based at Stanford University. The group offers free private lessons and music theory tutoring to students. Started in 1998 as a part of the Stanford Alliance for Service Through the Arts, MELODY grew to include approximately twenty Stanford tutors per year, serving roughly twenty-five elementary school students, but took a large hit during the pandemic. name: Muslim Student Union
description: To foster a spiritually enriching, inclusive, and supportive Muslim community at Stanford University; to engage critically with the diverse histories, cultures, and identities of Muslims; to serve as a representative voice for Muslim students, faculty, and staff; to promote unity, justice, and mutual understanding while upholding truth as a sacred trust, and building a center of academic, intellectual, and spiritual excellence that extends beyond campus to the broader national and global community.

name: National Organization for the Professional Advancement of Black Chemists and Chemical Engineers
description: The mission of NOBCChE@Stanford includes building a community of culturally conscious black scientists and engineers. NOBCChE@Stanford will strive toward professional, academic, and philanthropic development, both as individuals and as a chapter, by engaging in events and workshops with industry, Stanford University, and minority communities.

name: Next BioLeader
description: Next BioLeader is a student-led, Stanford-based network dedicated to empowering the next generation of scientists by expanding access to mentorship, professional development, and a collaborative community that supports diverse career paths in science.

name: Nexus Neurotech
description: We are an undergrad-led engineering group focused on making the burgeoning field of neurotechnology accessible to the Stanford community. Through industry connections, structured projects, seminars, and networking events we hope to inspire the next generation of neuro-engineers who will radically change the fabric of society.

name: Nigerian Grads at Stanford
description: Nigerian Grads at Stanford (NGS) exists to foster community among Nigerian graduate students and promote awareness of Nigerian culture within the broader Stanford community.

description: Stanford NAIJA is┬áNaija is a student-run organization whose mission is to educate and celebrate the deep beauty of Nigeria's diverse culture and heritage, and┬áfoster discussion and promote awareness of issues within Nigeria with fellow Stanford students and the neighboring communities. We host a variety of events, including Nollywood Movie Nights, Game Nights, Cooking Sessions, fireside chats with amazing speakers and more! name: Nikkei Student Union
description: The purpose of Nikkei Student Union is to provide a space for students to explore Nikkei and Japanese identity and build community through cultural, political, and social programming.

name: Noopur

We fuse styles of dance from across India, including Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Mohiniyattam, and Odissi, and add some of our own flair! We integrate classical tradition with contemporary themes to create unique, compelling pieces of art.

name: Notes from the Farm
description: Notes from the Farm aims to promote belonging on the Stanford campus as a whole, most specifically for the population of incoming freshmen every year. We aim to achieve this by gathering a diverse collection of stories from a variety of Stanford undergraduates and delivering the stories to each incoming class. The purpose of the NFTF organization is to produce the handbook. name: O-Tone
description: O-Tone is an all-gender East Asian-interest a cappella group. Our mission is to be a space for the celebration of East Asian culture and sharing of stories through song. Through our renditions of East Asian language pop and traditional music, as well as English-language music by Asian artists, we hope to spread awareness of the diversity of East Asian and Asian-American culture and provide a creative outlet for those interested in East Asian and Asian-American music. name: Olami @ Stanford
description: Olami @ Stanford fills a unique niche on campus by enriching students' Jewish education through authentic, immersive study of classic Jewish religious texts and the application of Jewish ethics to the modern world. Olami @ Stanford provides students with the opportunity to immerse themselves in a traditional Jewish learning environment, where they can thoughtfully engage with life's deepest questions and explore the enduring relevance of ancient Jewish wisdom for today's leaders.

name: Orthodox Christian Campus Ministries
description: To nurture the spiritual growth of Oriental Orthodox Christian students and to promote understanding of the Oriental Orthodox faith on campus.

name: Orthodox Christian Students Association at Stanford
description: The Orthodox Christian Students Association at Stanford offers students the opportunity to learn about Orthodox Christianity through weekly meetings and fellowship opportunities throughout the academic quarter. All those interested in learning about Orthodoxy, including non-Orthodox, are welcome! Our vision and purpose is as follows: 1. To bring together Orthodox Christian students at Stanford. 2. name: Out in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics at Stanford
description: Out in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics is a Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Two-Spirited, Queer, Questioning, Intersex, Asexual (LGBTTQQIA) + Ally affirming organization that aims to provide services and support for students in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics and to create a dynamic network between students and professionals in industry and academia.

name: Pacific Islander Student Association
description: The purpose of the Pacific Islander Student Association is to learn, share, practice and celebrate the Indigenous cultural knowledge and history of Oceania. PISA provides a hub for Indigenous Pacific Islanders to meet and empower one another, as well as educate the Stanford community and bring awareness to Pasifika cultures and traditions.

name: Pakistanis at Stanford
description: PaS seeks to create a community for all Pakistani students and any students interested in Pakistani culture.

name: Parakaleo Christian Ministries
description: Parakaleo Christian Ministries is a student group focused on teaching the foundations of Biblical counseling. Parakaleo offers a three-quarter course on Biblical counseling with the goal of teaching students to apply God's written word to their own daily life issues and relationships, and equipping them to counsel others from the Bible under the guidance and empowering of the Holy Spirit. Led by advisors Steve and Erica Lawry.

name: Parallax
description: Parallax broadens Stanford medical students’ exposure to disciplines often overlooked in traditional clinical training, venture, innovation, systems thinking, and contemplative practice. By cultivating the “MD-plus” and “physician-plus” mindset, Parallax enables interdisciplinary dialogue and empowers future clinicians to build more innovative, resilient, and system-aware careers in healthcare.

name: People for Animal Welfare
description: People for Animal Welfare (PAW)'s mission is to create a tight-knit community of animal lovers on campus who work towards reducing animal suffering and raising awareness of animal welfare issues on campus.

name: Persian Student Association
description: The Persian Student Association is a non-political volunteer student organization which shall respect the religious identities of all its members and whose objective shall be to sponsor Persian social and cultural activities and events, to promote an understanding of Persian culture, to help foster friendship among different cultural groups, and to provide a source of union and support for the Persian community at Stanford.

name: Physics Undergraduate Women and Gender Minorities at Stanford
description: Our two main missions are to 1. Promote diversity in Physics by uniting and uplifting minority voices. 2. Provide opportunities for personal, academic, and career development.

name: Pilipino American Student Union
description: Through service, education, leadership, mentorship, and outreach within and outside of Stanford University, the Pilipinx American Student Union strives to maintain a safe space for Pilipinx-American students and allies to: empower youth to act as agents of positive change, explore personal and collective Pilipinx identity, celebrate the richness of Pilipinx and Pilipinx-American culture, nurture the spirit of a supportive and thriving family.

name: Polish Students at Stanford
description: The Polish Student Association at Stanford exists to create a supportive and inclusive community for students connected to Poland. We bring together Polish international students, individuals exploring their Polish roots, and anyone interested in Polish culture, history, and identity. By fostering mentorship, friendship, and cultural exchange, we aim to celebrate Polish heritage while helping members feel at home at Stanford.

name: Puerto Rican Student Organization
description: The purpose of this organization is threefold: to promote education of the Puerto Rican culture across campus, provide a home for those 3,600 miles away from home, and foster professional growth and unity across academic domains.

name: Quiz Bowl Club
description: Compete with teams from other universities in Quiz Bowl, a fast-paced buzzer-based competition testing academic knowledge of many fields.

name: Ram's Head Theatrical Society
description: Ram's Head is a campus-wide, student-run theatrical organization dedicated to fostering the production of original works and providing quality artistic, educational, and community experiences for its members and the Stanford community.

name: Reformed University Fellowship at Stanford
description: Know, Love, Serve Jesus at Stanford in community.

name: Rem at Stanford
description: Rem at Stanford is on a mission to keep doors open and dreams alive for small businesses in the Bay Area. Through pro-bono consulting projects, Rem at Stanford creates an immersive curriculum shaping students and young problem-solvers into the next generation of impact-driven innovators. Rem at Stanford is a way for students to develop new personal and professional relationships, engage in unique hands-on learning experiences, and–most of all–positively impact their community.

name: Restorative Film Collective
description: Restorative Film Collective is a creative collective of filmmakers, writers, and artists of color creating art that deconstructs traditionally white filmmaking and reimagines a radical future. We seek to create a space of collaboration and cultural care for marginalized people in creative fields, opening space for us to flourish in the arts — whether that's as actors, writers, directors, editors or designers. name: Robber Barons Sketch Comedy
description: We are an audition-based collective of writers and performers who collaborate in producing free sketch comedy shows for the Stanford student body on a quarterly basis. Among our members, our mission is to provide a community for those interested in comedy and a creative outlet. On campus, that mission extends to providing free entertainment and participating in the network of student-led groups devoted to fostering creativity and providing opportunities in the arts.

name: Russian-speaking Student Association
description: We are devoted to build a community of Russian-speaking people and people interested in the Russian language, promote culture and have fun!

name: Sahaja Yoga Stanford
description: Sahaja Yoga Stanford (SYS) is dedicated to promoting mental health, well-being, and spiritual growth through the principles and techniques of Sahaja Yoga Meditation (SYM). Our mission is to foster a holistic understanding of the mind–body–spirit connection, cultivate self-awareness, and support the integration of mental, emotional, and spiritual well-being, drawing on both interspiritual perspectives and scientific insights. We aim to provide Stanford students with accessible, experiential tools for personal growth, resilience, and community connection.

name: SBSBZ: Stanford Bachata Sensual and Brazilian Zouk
description: The purpose of SBSBZ is to enrich the Stanford cultural experience through deep, connection-based social Latin dancing while understanding the mechanics of solid technique. It is our experience that one can co-create a dance experience with any lead and follow. Our foundation is Bachata Sensual—created by renowned artists Korke and Judith—a dance based on tested lead and follow principles of natural energy motion and strong partner connection, incorporating elements of rhythmic gymnastics, salsa, traditional bachata, contemporary dance, and more.

name: Scholars of Finance
description: Scholars of Finance (SOF) seeks to create an inclusive atmosphere where members practice integrity, humility, compassion, and excellence.

name: Science Policy Group at Stanford
description: The Stanford Science Policy Group (SSPG) aims to create a central hub to engage and educate scientists/non-scientists in policy, provide students with tools for science policy professional development, expose students to thoughtful speakers that work in various sectors of policy development (legislative, legal, local etc.), and collaborate with other science policy related groups at Stanford and across the country.

name: Scrubs Addressing the Firearms Epidemic at Stanford
description: As future professionals, medical and beyond, we view the gun violence epidemic in America as a healthcare concern, one that poses immense risks to us and our communities. We seek to work with medical professionals to do what we can to educate ourselves and our peers to help reduce the detrimental effects of the epidemic ultimately supporting the wellbeing of all.

name: Service-Oriented Audio Production Notes
description: The purpose of SOAP Notes is to utilize music performance and production as a form of service, enriching the lives of individuals interfacing with the healthcare system, including but not limited to patients and their families, long-term care facility residents, and healthcare providers. After connecting with and learning about their music interests, SOAP Notes members will work together with each individual to produce music tailored to them and send it as a lasting gift that they and their families can treasure for life. name: Sexual Health Peer Resources Center
description: We are Stanford's Sexual Health Peer Resource Center. A safe space for Stanford affiliates to explore sex education, positivity, resources, and more! We offer a quarterly course on comprehensive sexual health education and peer counseling skills (Wellness 191) & engage in the community via outreach events and by vending highly subsidized resources.

name: Shaku
description: Shaku is a dance group dedicated to innovative and exploratory choreography and performance, drawing influences from styles across various countries and cultures within the African Diaspora.

name: Sikh Students Association at Stanford
description: The Sikh Student Association at Stanford (SSA) is dedicated to fostering a vibrant and inclusive community that embraces the values, principles, and rich heritage of Sikhi. We strive to create an empowering environment where Sikh students and allies can connect, learn, and grow together. Through our mission, the Sikh Student Association at Stanford seeks to build bridges of understanding, empower individuals, and contribute to a more compassionate and just society. description: Our a cappella aims at: 1. Enhance the appreciation of Chinese contemporary music and thus, Chinese language and culture in general; 2. Add to the cultural richness of the Stanford music community by combining the Western musical form of a cappella and Chinese Music; 3. Give performances on campus at various activities as well as off-campus within the Stanford community; 4. Give students of Chinese background or those who like Chinese culture and music a chance to show their talent.

name: Singaporeans at Stanford
description: Singaporeans @ Stanford aims to connect Singaporean students through hosting fun activities through the year, to make this community feel like home!

name: SLS American Constitution Society
description: The American Constitution Society for Law and Policy is a national organization of law students, law professors, judges, practicing lawyers and others. We want to counter the dominant vision of American law, a narrow conservative vision that lacks appropriate regard for the ways in which the law affects people's lives. name: SLS Asian Pacific Islander Law Student Association
description: APILSA is a long-standing law school organization that promotes and advocates for the interests of Asian and Pacific Islander (API) law students as well as the larger Asian and Pacific Islander communities at Stanford. APILSA coordinates get- togethers and mentorship programs, provides academic assistance and professional advice to students, and works with the law school administration and other student groups to foster an inclusive and welcoming community for API law students. Additionally, we provide programming on the intersections of API issues and the law.

name: SLS Black Law Students Association
description: The Stanford Black Law Student Association (BLSA) is a student-run organization that strives to provide career and academic support for students of African descent and their allies. The group also serves to forge alliances among BLSA members, alumni, faculty of color, and other law students in the Bay Area. We provide a space for students to engage with issues impacting black communities, both through discussion and community service. description: SLS Christian Legal Fellowship is a community of Stanford Law School students dedicated to integrating Christian faith with the study and practice of law. CLF members seek to explore and grow in their faith, to encourage discussions on religious topics, to assert a high standard of legal ethics, and to promote religious freedom.

It is founded on the principles that the state exists to preserve freedom, that the separation of governmental powers is central to our Constitution, and that it is emphatically the province and duty of the judiciary to say what the law is, not what it should be.

The club builds community within this joint degree program as well as the wider Stanford community, and also attempts to relate the experiences of our club members with opportunities unique to the skills we are developing at Stanford.

name: SLS Jewish Law Student Association
description: JLSA is committed to creating and maintaining a community for Jewish students at Stanford Law School, advocating for the Jewish community within Stanford University and the legal profession, and sending highly qualified, dedicated, and responsible Jewish lawyers into every legal arena.

description: The SLS Law and Political Economy (LPE) group is part of the larger LPE movement, which is a network of scholars, practitioners, and students advancing a legal paradigm rooted in the reality that politics and economics cannot be separated–and that the law is vital in shaping both. LPE centers questions of political economy to confront present-day crises such as regional and racial inequality; ecological devastation; and unaccountable corporate power. NALSA welcomes all members of the Stanford University community. We aim to foster an environment of openness and thoughtful debate surrounding issues of concern to Indian country, where all opinions and perspectives are treated with respect.

description: The purpose of OWLS is to provide a social network and support for students with more life experience than the average law student. OWLS organizes social events for members, as well as career talks and other events that address issues of unique interest to older and mid-career law students. OWLS is open to all SLS students without discrimination as to age or other factors.
