description: Stanford Engineering Research Introductions Organization (SERIO) is an organization where graduate students can come together to empower students early in their undergraduate career, particularly freshmen and sophomores from underrepresented communities, to pursue graduate academic engineering research.

name: Stanford Ethiopian and Eritrean Student Association
description: The goal of the Stanford Ethiopian and Eritrean Student Association is to provide a community where students can gather together to learn about, share, and spread awareness about Ethiopian, Eritrean, Sudanese, South Sudanese, Somali, and Somaliland culture and history.

name: Stanford Etiquette Club
description: To foster a culture of respect, professionalism, and social grace at Stanford by equipping students with essential etiquette skills for navigating personal, social, and professional interactions. Through workshops, events, and discussions, we aim to empower members to build confidence, strengthen connections, and leave a lasting positive impact in every sphere of life.

name: Stanford Film Society
description: To endow the Stanford community with a culture of film appreciation through regular screenings.

name: Stanford Finance
description: Stanford Finance's mission is to facilitate the entry and success of Stanford students in the finance industry via education, preparation, and the building of a global professional network.

name: Stanford Fleet Street Singers
description: Stanford's Premier Comedy A Cappella group, bringing music and laughter to the Stanford Community since 1981.

name: Stanford Flight Club
description: Stanford Flight Club will foster a safe and fun environment where undergraduate and graduate students come together to learn, innovate, build and fly Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), focusing on civilian applications. These activities will draw from many disciplines across Stanford University by encouraging students to leverage their classroom knowledge from areas including but not limited to aerodynamics, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, and other disciplines related to the design, analysis, construction, and application of UAVs (fixed wing, drones, etc.).

name: Stanford Flow Arts
description: We aim to provide resources for and foster a community where interested students can practice and perform flow arts. What is flow arts, you ask? Flow arts are a form of creative expression that combine elements of dance and prop manipulation. Common props that we use in our club include LED and fabric poi, staffs, optic fiber whips, Levi-wands, rope darts, fans, gymnastic ribbons, and many others to create visually captivating patterns and rhythms.

name: Stanford Fly Fishing and Tying Club
description: The Stanford Fly Fishing and Tying club was established to share the joy and benefits of fly fishing with the Stanford community. Our goal is to promote the sport through education, conservation, service, and involvement. Our mission as a club is threefold: 1) To spread awareness of fly fishing not only as a sport, but as a form of relaxation, mindfulness, and art by hosting outings, workshops, and meetings to educate our community. 2) Promote conservation by engaging with local ecologists and conservation groups to preserve California's pristine trout waters. 3) Utilize the resources of Stanf

name: Stanford Funbotics X STEM Nights
description: Stanford STEM Nights aims to encourage K-12 students to develop their interests in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics by hosting science nights at underserved elementary and middle schools where students will be able to engage with Stanford students leading various science experiments and activities. The organization will also mentor middle and high school students working on science fair projects and organize an annual Invention Convention or Maker Convention where aspiring engineers and innovators can showcase their work and learn from their peers.

name: Stanford Funk Club
description: Stanford Funk Club's mission is to build a community to support student musicians in the creation and development of funk/soul/RnB/pop music.

name: Stanford Game Development
description: This club provides a community space for game designers at Stanford (e.g., artists, programmers, sound designers, and storywriters) to meet and collaborate on game-related projects. We also are a source of learning about analog and digital ways of making.

name: Stanford Genetic Counseling Student Interest Group
description: Stanford's Genetic Counseling Student Interest Group (GC SIG) is a student group run by both undergraduates and current Stanford Genetic Counseling Students. We put on events for students who are interested in learning more about genetic counseling or genetics in general, we lead workshops for those in the process of applying to GC programs, and we connect students with resources and information about the profession. We are always expanding and putting new ideas into action, and we invite everyone to come learn more!

name: Stanford German Student Association
description: The Stanford German Student Association was founded in 1997 to provide a forum for Stanford affiliates with an interest in German language and culture. We bring together and strengthen the German and German-interested community at Stanford, including its extensive alumni network in Silicon Valley and Germany. Through social events, knowledge-sharing sessions, and networking evenings, the SGSA fosters the exchange of ideas between Silicon Valley and Germany, connects Stanford students to career paths in Germany, and promotes German cultural values within the Stanford community.

name: Stanford Girls Run Club
description: The mission of the Stanford Girls Run Club is to provide a welcoming space for girls and other students to develop a love for running.

name: Stanford Gospel Choir
description: The Stanford Gospel Choir is a biblically based organization whose purpose is to minister through various forms of gospel music. The Stanford Gospel Choir has been bringing the gospel of Jesus Christ through song to the Stanford community and surrounding Bay Area since 1978. Though this unique cultural ministry of gospel music is deeply rooted in the African American tradition, the choir includes a diverse group of believers from different ethnic and cultural backgrounds. The SGC is open to all students, staff and faculty This non-audition group seeks to represent Christ through Gospel music,

name: Stanford Graduate Founders
description: We empower Stanford's graduate student founders by fostering an ecosystem of interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation through tailored mixers, events, workshops and our flagship Demo Day event for over 1,500 attendees. We nurture a supportive community (Currently over 1,000+ graduate founders!) where students can find cofounders, share resources, and kickstart their entrepreneurial journeys, turning visionary ideas into impactful realities. Website: https://stanfordfounders.stanford.edu/

name: Stanford Graduate Society of Women Engineers
description: The Stanford Graduate Society of Women Engineers (GradSWE) seeks to promote the study of engineering through outreach, provide professional development opportunities, and enhance the diversity of the Stanford Engineering community by focusing upon the needs and interests of its female graduate students.

name: Stanford Harmonics
description: The mission of the Stanford Harmonics is to bring innovative, high-quality rock and experimental a cappella to the Stanford community through both live performances and recorded music.

name: Stanford Hawai'i Club
description: To bring a unique and diverse community perspective to the broader student body and foster an extensive support system for students with ties to Hawaii and the Pacific Islands. Our club will foster community within and throughout the Bay Area, aiming to spread aloha to all.

name: Stanford Healthcare Design Challenge
description: The Stanford Healthcare Design Challenge, the first of its kind, sources international talent and directs them toward addressing critical issues in healthcare. Not only is this the first healthcare design competition at Stanford, where we may leverage the incredible entrepreneurial spirit of Silicon Valley, but it is also an opportunity to pioneer a new model for academic competitions. name: Stanford Housing Equity Project
description: The Stanford Housing Equity Project exists to connect resources of Silicon Valley and higher academia to community initiatives supporting low-income and unsheltered residents to housing and social support through establishing high-quality programming and long-term organizational capacity.

name: Stanford Hydrogen Club
description: The purpose of the club is threefold: To connect students with diverse backgrounds who share a deep interest for hydrogen, to establish connections with key industry players, and thirdly, to serve as an educational hub for hydrogen and its potential in shaping a decarbonized energy future.

name: Stanford iGEM
description: Stanford International Genetically Engineered Machine (iGEM) is dedicated to the advancement of synthetic biology through student-driven research, education, competition, and the development of an open and collaborative community. The organization brings together multidisciplinary Stanford students to design, build, and test cutting-edge biological solutions to real world problems, ultimately working towards representing Stanford in the Grand Jamboree Competition that bring together thousands of students, leaders in the industry, and stakeholders to shape the future of synthetic biology.

name: Stanford Improvisors
description: The Stanford Improvisors aim to provide quality improvisational theater performances to the Stanford community and to foster a greater interest in and exposure to the art of improv.

name: Stanford In Government
description: Stanford in Government is a nonpartisan, student-run organization that promotes political awareness and involvement on the Stanford campus. SIG is committed to engaging students and the greater community in the governmental process through encouraging campus awareness of political issues, strengthening community service efforts, and providing internship resources and fellowships.

name: Stanford India Association
description: Stanford India Association (SIA) aims to provide a window into the multiple facets of India as a nation and as a cultural entity with a rich history. As a genial community of students at Stanford University, SIA will attempt to bring together students with an interest in acquiring knowledge about and having a desire to participate in events about India's current affairs, nationally acclaimed events, secular celebrations and events that promote the imparting of cultural knowledge

name: Stanford India Economic and Policy Club
description: Stanford India Policy and Economics Club (SIPEC) is a student-led organization at Stanford University focused on fostering high-impact dialogue on the evolving U.S.-India partnership among the Stanford community.

name: Stanford Indigenous Students of the AmericaS
description: As Indigenous students from across the Americas and the Caribbean, we want to empower the voices of our cultures on Stanford's campus. We aim to prevail and assert our intergenerational identities. We want all indigenous groups to be included, so our community continues growing, embracing their pride in their roots and the intersectionalities of our cultures and stories.

name: Stanford Initiative for Domestic Abuse Prevention
description: Our mission is two-fold: (1) nurture strong, healthy family foundations in an effort to prevent domestic violence from occurring and (2) foster a new generation of informed, proactive leaders to help prevent domestic violence.

name: Stanford Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
description: Stanford IEEE is Stanford's student chapter of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE). IEEE's core purpose is to foster technological innovation and excellence for the benefit of humanity.

name: Stanford Irish Association
description: The Stanford Irish Association has, since its foundation, had a tripartite mission. First, to engage and mentor Irish citizens at Stanford. We aim to provide support for Irish students, faculty, and staff transitioning to America and/or the Bay Area. Second, to provide a forum for those with Irish heritage to come together with those with an interest in Ireland to share and promote Irish culture, language, people, and history. name: Stanford Israel Association
description: The Stanford Israel Association (SIA) strives to celebrate and share the unique culture of the State of Israel with members of the Stanford community, including those who are otherwise unaware of Israel. As an organization, SIA promotes and defends the existence of a vibrant, safe, secure and democratic Jewish State. Furthermore, SIA honors and welcomes the breadth of opinions and perspectives regarding Israel's successful future and its personal significance to diverse individuals.

name: Stanford Italian Society
description: Promoting Italian culture and traditions at Stanford since 2013.

description: The Stanford Jail and Prison Education Program (SJPEP) provides educational support and programming to incarcerated community members in Bay Area jails, where many are spending over 10+ years in facilities without adequate programming and services. name: Stanford Jewish Voice for Peace
description: Jewish Voice for Peace provides a meaningful space for Jewish students to find community beyond Zionism, and an outlet through which to fight for Palestinian liberation. We are here as a home for Jews at Stanford who stand against our institution's complicity in genocide, apartheid, dehumanization, extractionism, and imperialism. Each of us have unique lived experiences with Judaism and Zionism - these diverse perspectives are vital to strengthening our contingent, and to gaining clarity on our purpose within the Stanford divestment movement and the broader struggle for collective liberation.

name: Stanford Journal of Art and Art History - Manicule
description: The Stanford Journal of Art History publishes exemplary undergraduate scholarship on art historical theory and practice annually. Our mission is to provide a platform for emerging voices in the field, promoting awareness of diverse art historical perspectives, facilitating critical discussions, and advancing the study of art in its cultural, historical, and theoretical (and practical?contexts. We aim to inspire a broader appreciation of art’s role in shaping societies and challenge traditional narratives within the discipline.

name: Stanford Kayak Club
description: The Stanford Kayak Club promotes the safe enjoyment of the sport of whitewater kayaking within the Stanford community. The club delivers on-campus kayaking instruction, organizes Common Adventure kayaking trips for members, and provides a forum for interested members who want to meet paddlers with similar skill levels.

description: Stanford Kids in Nutrition is a student-led organization dedicated to enhancing food equity and improving long-term health outcomes for youth and families through nutrition education and food literacy. In partnership with the national Kids in Nutrition organization, Stanford Kids in Nutrition equips children with foundational knowledge about nutrition and food systems so they can make informed, sustainable food choices that promote lifelong health, prevent chronic disease, and advance health equity.

name: Stanford Knitting Circle
description: The Stanford Knitting Circle aims to bring together students from across campus to explore and celebrate the art of knitting and other fiber/textile crafts, such as crochet. Our mission is to create a welcoming community for knitters where they can share and exchange skills, foster their creativity, and form new connections and friendships. We hope to not only create a safe space for existing knitters, but for those with no prior experience who are interested in learning in an accessible environment.

name: Stanford Latino
description: Stanford Latino strives to support its members as they prepare to become agents of change for their home countries and abroad.

name: Stanford Latino Medical School Association Plus
description: LMSA Plus is dedicated to empowering undergraduate students who aspire to careers in healthcare by providing mentorship, professional development, and networking opportunities. As the undergraduate chapter of the Latino Medical Student Association (LMSA), we are committed to fostering an inclusive community that supports the academic and personal growth of Latina/o/x and other underrepresented students. description: The Stanford Lean Club was cofounded by Brando Miranda and Henry Bosch and is a student-run organization focused on the formalization of mathematics and software in Lean. We believe that formal verification is the future of mathematics and software engineering, and we are dedicated to making it accessible to students and researchers at Stanford.

name: Stanford Light Opera Company
description: SLOCo is a group of musicians dedicated to the exploration and production of opera, operetta, and lyric theatre. It will provide experiences similar to those at Lunar New Year celebrations and Buddhist religious events.

name: Stanford Middle East Ensemble
description: To promote Middle Eastern music, diversity and cross cultural awareness on campus in a respectful and traditional manner through educational events and performances on Stanford campus and in the broader Bay Area.

name: Stanford Mixology Club
description: The Stanford Mixology Club aims to connect students across campus with a shared interest in learning about the art, history, and science of drink-making. We aim to connect the Stanford community through engaging events, including workshops on fermentation of non-alcoholic drinks, drink-making techniques, and seasonal Californian ingredients, as well as social gatherings featuring non-alcoholic fermented drinks. By exploring the historical roots of drinks—from apothecaries to modern mixology—and hosting expert speakers, we foster curiosity, creativity, and meaningful connections across campus.

name: Stanford Mock Trial
description: Mock trial is a competitive activity that simulates a trial in court. Each school prepares its own witnesses and attorneys, and then presents their case against other schools in front of judges and scorers who determine the winner. name: Stanford Moonshot Club

Furthermore, we inspire and educate the community through speaker events and educational workshops.

name: Stanford Muslim Medical Association
description: The Stanford Muslim Medical Association (SMMA) strives to foster a spiritually nurturing, tolerant, and inclusive Muslim community at the Stanford School of Medicine and affiliated hospitals. The SMMA strives to maintain regular service activities, active mentorship programs, and educational programming.

description: Stanford Myanmar Student Association (SMSA) aims to provide a community space for those of Myanmar descent and their allies to learn and grow in their knowledge about Myanmar. description: Stanford Native American Graduate Students (SNAGS) is committed to providing academic, professional and cultural resources to the American Indian, First Nations, Alaska Natives, and Native Hawaiian graduate communities at Stanford. We bring Native students together to build a sense of community while educating each other and the broader Stanford Community about our research, identities, and ideas.

description: The Stanford Nutrition Society is a student-led organization dedicated to creating an inclusive and supportive space where students from all backgrounds can explore nutrition science together and engage in open conversations about how it connects to everyday life. We aim to foster welcoming, evidence-based peer discussions that build confidence, critical thinking, and practical understanding of nutrition in a collaborative and low-pressure environment. We aim to make Stanford feel more like home by fostering connection, belonging, and pride in our diverse Peruvian identity.

name: Stanford Powwow

We aim to build community within Stanford's Native student population, along with provide an enriching experience into Native cultures for all students, the Stanford community and public.

name: Stanford Practical Ethics Club
description: To cultivate empathetic, thoughtful discussion on difficult ethical issues, and to help students think about how to apply ethics in their daily lives.

name: Stanford Pre-Business Association
description: Stanford Pre-Business Association prepares its members for professional opportunities in five pillars of business: consulting, finance, marketing, technology, and social impact. We provide unmatched accessibility to resources and opportunities, flexibility in exploring various aspects of business within the five pillars and beyond, and a great community to learn from and befriend. We offer practical workshops to build students' business knowledge, hands-on client projects to develop real-world project experience, and networking opportunities to connect students to prestigious firms and alumni.

name: Stanford Pre-Law Society
description: The Stanford Pre-Law Society (SPLS) is a student organization dedicated to bringing together Stanford undergraduates who are interested in the law and in pursuing legal careers. We are a community of like-minded students who wish to help members of the student body reach informed decisions about their futures. In addition to programming, we work with Undergraduate Advising and Research (UAR) and other campus organizations to build community, understanding, and a common vision.

description: SPN is dedicated to bridging the professional opportunity gap for transfers, non-traditional students, and any undergrads interested in accelerating their professional exploration. By providing industry specific career prep and an accelerated project-based “innovation-lab”, SPN ensures that students on a compressed academic timeline have the tools, experience, and network necessary to successfully transition into high-impact careers.

name: Stanford Public Interest Technology Lab (Stanford PIT Lab)
description: The PIT Lab focuses on the systems and structures that shape technology’s development, closely examining what it actually means for technology to be built in the public interest. By fostering an interdisciplinary and diverse community around PIT at Stanford, we aim to promote more reflection and advocacy around technology’s role in society.

name: Stanford Quantum Computing Association
description: The Stanford Quantum Computing Association's purpose and mission is to educate the Stanford community and beyond about quantum computing and to develop the future scientists and engineers involved in quantum computing and related fields.

name: Stanford Queer & Asian
description: Stanford Queer & Questioning Asians & Pacific Islanders (Q&A) aims to provide space for folks to meet, have fun, and engage critically with issues at the intersection of API and queer/trans identities. We also build bridges and create cohesion across queer communities in the Bay Area.

description: Stanford Raagapella is an all-gender South Asian focus a cappella group. Stanford Raagapella's goal is to unite members and audiences and to encourage the appreciation of music from South Asia and other cultures by capturing the essences and energy of music in performance and recording. Stanford ROTC serves to support cadets/midshipmen in Army ROTC (at Santa Clara University), Air Force and Space Force ROTC (at San Jose State University), and Navy and Marine Corps ROTC (at UC Berkeley) programs.

description: Founded in 1989, South Asian Society has expanded quickly to become one of the largest cultural groups at Stanford. With over 600 members, SAS functions as a portal that connects the Stanford community to South Asian culture. By exploring history and tradition, addressing issues of sociopolitical importance, presenting a social forum for our members, and promoting our performances and lively arts to the rest of the Stanford community, SAS seeks to strengthen student awareness of South Asian culture.

name: Stanford Spanish Student Association
description: The Spanish Student Association aims to build a strong community among Spanish students at Stanford and to bring the Spanish culture, language, and traditions to the broader Stanford campus through inclusive social, cultural, and professional programming.

name: Stanford Spoken Word Collective
description: The Stanford Spoken Word Collective is a student organization at Stanford University dedicated to cultivating exquisite emotion both within and without ourselves to generate explosive written and spoken poetry. The Collective functions both as a community and as the primary logistical and funding body for Stanford's slam and spoken word intercollegiate relationships. We are a family of poets that performs at campus events, community programs, and other spoken word events. We also hold quarterly shows, bring artists to campus, and host writing workshops. name: Stanford Sports Analytics Club
description: To provide a discussion space for those interested in an analytical approach to sports, to support projects on analytical questions in sports, and to provide insight into careers in sports analytics.

name: Stanford Stand-Up Comedy Club
description: Building a supportive and inclusive space for students at all experience levels to: Develop stand-up skills and material through workshops focused on joke writing, delivery, and stage presence Gain on-stage experience and build a stand-up portfolio through regular performances at open mics, quarterly showcases, and other Stanford events Network with local comedy professionals and venues to create opportunities for mentorship, off-campus performances, and industry connections

name: Stanford Storyboard Club
description: To promote creative expression through visual storytelling (including, but not limited to, storyboarding) and artmarking among the Stanford community.

name: Stanford Student Biodesign & Biopharma
description: SSB's overarching mission is to cultivate and support an environment of healthcare innovation for students in engineering, design, and pre-health disciplines. We aim to connect members with advising, mentorship, and opportunities in biomedical innovation, as well as expose students to different pathways to biomedical innovation. Our goal is to empower students with the tools and experiences to build for healthcare.

name: Stanford Student Biotechnology Group
description: A nexus between Stanford and our partners in the biotech ecosystem: We support Stanford graduate and professional students, postdocs, and other affiliates from the biosciences, medicine, engineering, business, and law, who are interested in biotech research, business, management, entrepreneurship, consulting, investing, and more. Our goal is to help individuals explore opportunities and build industry connections in biotech by creating avenues for experiential education, career development, and networking. We are committed to promoting racial and gender equity in biotech as we serve and repres

name: Stanford Student Parents in Academia
description: Creating a community for student parents to navigate and support through our academic and parenting journey.

name: Stanford Student Space Initiative
description: Giving future leaders of the space industry the hands-on experience and broader insight they need to realize the next era of space development.

name: Stanford Students for Justice in Palestine
description: 1) Students for Justice in Palestine (SJP) is a diverse group of students, faculty, staff, and community members at Stanford University, organized on principles to promote justice, human rights, liberation, and self-determination for the Palestinian people. 2) SJP is a space comprised of both Palestinian and non-Palestinian students, engaged in self-determination and solidarity, respectively. Within SJP, we defer to the leadership and vision of Palestinian students whenever possible. 3) SJP views the liberation of the Palestinian people as bound up with the liberation of all oppressed people.

name: Stanford Students for Life
description: Our mission is to educate the Stanford community about pro-life issues, to provide support for those facing difficult life-related decisions, and to defend the basic human rights of the unborn, the very elderly, and all others whose lives are unjustly in danger of being deemed dispensable by our society.

name: Stanford Students for Rare
description: Our mission is to raise awareness of the unique challenges faced by individuals and families affected by rare diseases through advocacy, education, and research here on campus and beyond.

name: Stanford Students In Entertainment
description: Stanford Students in Entertainment (SSIE) is a pre-professional organization to help Stanford students build careers in the entertainment industry. Through industry panels, networking trips to Los Angeles, alumni mentorship, and hands-on workshops, SSIE helps students explore career paths in film, television, music, digital media, and more.

name: Stanford Students Palestinian Association
description: Our purpose is to foster a supportive community for Palestinian students by promoting awareness of Palestinian culture, addressing issues specific to Palestinian identity, advocating for the needs of the Palestinian community at Stanford, and providing a space for social connection and identity exploration outside of the political sphere.

name: Stanford SupplyHer
description: The purpose of this organization is to bring together students with a passion for art and give them a space to use their creativity to uplift women by utilizing artistic passion in parallel to philanthropic action. We will also collect donations of sanitary products for women's shelters and health centers, as well as promote education of menstrual health and advertise existing resources to combat period poverty.

name: Stanford Surf
description: Stanford Surf aims to create a centralized community that values the sport of surfing, the protection of our oceans, and the celebration of surfing cultures around the world. We aim to increase accessibility to surfing for all communities on the Stanford campus, prioritizing diversity, equity, and inclusion. We would like to welcome any surfers and surf enthusiasts alike, regardless of skill level, to join us as we create a stoked Stanford. YEWW!

name: Stanford Sustainable Investment Group
description: Stanford Sustainable Investment Group’s mission is to empower undergraduates to explore how business and innovation can drive climate solutions. We build a dedicated community at the intersection of climate and business through hands-on programs, unique events, applied research projects, and real-world engagement with leading industry partners.

name: Stanford Swing Dancers
description: Stanford Swing Dancers provides a community for Stanford's swing dancers by hosting classes, workshops, and a place to dance for those who already love or want to learn more about swing dancing.

name: Stanford Symbolic Systems Society
description: We strive to create an enriching community for students, faculty and alumni interested in the interdisciplinary study of Symbolic Systems!

name: Stanford Symphony Orchestra
description: Providing outstanding opportunities for the practice and enjoyment of orchestral music.

name: Stanford Synapse: Brain Injury Support Group
description: The mission of Stanford Synapse: Brain Injury Support Group is twofold: 1) to provide Stanford students with an opportunity to serve as leaders within the local community and learn about the patient perspective of living with a brain injury 2) to provide individuals with brain injuries with support, exposure to additional resources, and opportunities to connect with and learn from one another Our organization accomplishes this by fostering the formation of supportive relationships between undergraduates and individuals with brain injury (BI).

name: Stanford Synthetic Biology Community
description: The purpose of the Stanford Synthetic Biology Community is to establish a space for synthetic biologists across departments and disciplines to share their research and interest in synthetic biology and form new collaborations. We recognized that undergraduate and graduate students at Stanford were developing and utilizing amazing synthetic biology tools across disciplines, for applications related to climate, sustainability, human health, and design, and have identified that creating a community to communicate and connect about science addresses this gap.

name: Stanford Tabletop Games Club
description: The Stanford Tabletop Games Club's mission is to provide accessibility to the vast world of tabletop games, whether they take place over several years or several hours. We welcome newcomers to the genre and match them with game runners through biquarterly meetings while also promoting a greater community outside of individual games where anyone can share ideas, receive feedback, and otherwise meet plenty of fellow tabletop players.

name: Stanford Taiko
description: Stanford Taiko exists to perform taiko -- the art of Japanese American drumming -- and educate Stanford and the wider community about the art form.

name: Stanford Taiwanese Student Association
description: The main goal for the organization is to better assist Taiwanese student community in aspects of living, academics, career and social networking. We work to connect Taiwanese students on campus, in Silicon Valley and in the greater bay area; to help international students settle down and find a sense of belonging on campus; to inclusively promote Taiwanese culture to broader student communities on campus.

name: Stanford Tamil Sangam
description: To share Tamil culture, language, and community.

name: Stanford Tango Club
description: The Stanford Tango Clubs aims to provide quality instruction of Argentine Tango and a space to practice for students and Stanford community members! We hope to introduce students and faculty to both tango and also the greater Bay Area tango community by going to events throughout the Bay together.

name: Stanford Theater Laboratory
description: Theater Lab is a flexible artistic home for theater artists, providing a vehicle for producing intimate, contemporary, experimental theater that Stanford students want to do and see.

name: Stanford Trading
description: Stanford Trading seeks to educate students in the many different ways money is invested. We will be accessible and thorough, giving students practical experience so that one day they feel confident to invest their own money.

name: Stanford Transfers Network
description: The Stanford Transfer Network is a student organization devoted to fostering community within the transfer population at Stanford.

name: Stanford Turkish Student Association
description: Stanford Turkish Student Association (TSA) is a registered voluntary student organization at Stanford University. TSA aims to: Increase awareness of Turkish culture in the community of Stanford University; Increase awareness of the political, social and economic situation of the Republic of Turkey in the community of Stanford University; Provide a network for Turkish students at Stanford University. TSA holds different kinds of activities including, but not limited to, dinners, movie screenings, networking events, informative speeches, celebrations of culturally important days. Most activities

name: Stanford Turning Point USA
description: The Turning Point USA chapter at Stanford fosters thoughtful conversation and civic engagement among students through the principles of freedom, limited government, free markets, and American exceptionalism. We provide a welcoming space for open dialogue, respectful debate, and the exchange of ideas on campus. We aim to promote a deeper understanding of foundational American values such as individual liberty, fiscal responsibility, and personal responsibility through hosting guest speakers, organizing events, and facilitating peer-led discussions. As a part of the national TPUSA network, we ar

name: Stanford Undergraduate Association of Veterans
description: SUAV will serve as the primary student organization supporting community for student Veterans who are pursuing their undergraduate or coterminal Master's degrees. Additionally, SUAV will provide communication and transition resources to student veterans and their families.

name: Stanford Undergraduate Education Society
description: To create a community where students can learn about aspects of education and be prepared to think and act critically on the most pressing educational issues.

name: Stanford Undergraduate Hospice and Palliative Care
description: Our goal is to bring awareness and hands-on exposure towards end-of-life care to undergraduate students across campus. Students who volunteer with us will have the chance to meaningfully interact with patients and learn to compassionately care for adults and their families through our four initiatives.

name: Stanford Undergraduate Law Review
description: The Stanford Undergraduate Law Review (SULR) is a student-run legal publication focusing on law. We accept high-quality and insightful submissions that take legal perspectives on a wide range of issues, from arguments on specific court decisions, to doctrinal or theoretical legal scholarship, to interdisciplinary articles that address contemporary issues in politics, economics, and society with a legal focus. Undergraduate students from any school worldwide are eligible to submit.

name: Stanford Undergraduate Moot Court
description: SUMC’s purpose is to develop its members’ skills in oral advocacy, legal research, and brief-writing.

name: Stanford Undergraduate Neuroscience Society
description: Supported by the Wu Tsai Neurosciences Institute, SUNS aims to foster a supportive community on campus for undergraduate students interested in all branches of neuroscience.

name: Stanford Undergraduate Psychology Association
description: SUPA exists to keep undergraduates aware of important information regarding Stanford's psychology major, provide forums for the hundreds of undergraduates in the Department to get to know one another and provide a venue for undergraduate opinions and concerns.

name: Stanford Undergraduate Research Association
description: The Stanford Undergraduate Research Association (SURA) was founded in 2014 to fulfill an unmet need at Stanford – a community for undergraduates to discuss, collaborate, and to learn more about research. The quality of research conducted by undergraduates at Stanford made clear that Stanford needed an organization that would be a vital resource for student researchers. SURA provides a forum that connects seniors and freshmen, professors and students, and Stanford undergraduates and their peers around the world. Offering research opportunities, mentorship relationships, workshops, research-orie

name: Stanford Undergraduate Research Journal
description: Founded in 2001, the Stanford Undergraduate Research Journal (SURJ) is an annual, peer-reviewed publication of research articles from all academic fields. The mission of SURJ is to encourage, recognize, and reward intellectual activity beyond the classroom while providing a forum for the exchange of research and ideas. Our journal is run entirely by a staff team of Stanford undergraduate students, led by an Editor-in-Chief. SURJ publishes work produced by well-qualified students from all institutions. All submitted papers undergo review by SURJ's team of editors, who subsequently deliberate an

name: Stanford Undergraduates in Mechanical Engineering
description: To support mechanical engineering undergraduates through the specific communal, academic, and pre-professional challenges related to our major so that we can achieve our greatest potential for success in this field.

name: Stanford Underrepresented Pre-Medical Association for First-Generation/Low-Income Students
description: The purpose of SUPAFLI(Stanford Underrepresented Pre-Medical Association for First-Generation/Low-Income Students) is to empower first-generation, low-income, and underrepresented pre-med students through personalized mentorship, access to essential resources, and a supportive network. We aim to contribute to Stanford's mission of fostering a unified community of inclusion, respect, and excellence by addressing the specific challenges faced by FLI students in their journey toward a medical career.

name: Stanford University Graduate Latin American Student Organization
description: The Stanford Latin American Graduate Students Association believes there is an untapped opportunity to foster connections across graduate programs and build a strong support network that promotes personal and professional relationships. Our Mission We aim to achieve three core goals: Create a supportive community for Latin American graduate students at Stanford, bridging gaps across different programs. Serve as a platform for collaboration between students and Latin American organizations within Stanford and beyond. Promote Latin American cultures and highlight the region's role in shaping glo

name: Stanford University Mathematical Organization
description: The Stanford University Mathematical Organization is a student group whose goal is to promote interest in math and foster mathematical community on campus through activities that encourage interaction between students, faculty, and the wider community. We seek to create an environment in which students of many backgrounds feel welcome and supported in pursuing math. While focused on undergraduates, SUMO is open to all Stanford affiliates interested in mathematics, regardless of field of study.

name: Stanford University PA Student Association
description: Stanford University Physician Assistant Student Association, or SUPASA, acts as the official organization representing the student body of the Stanford MSPA Program. The SUPASA governance promotes academic achievement, student wellness, community, and clinical excellence of its current students in order to promote the physician assistant as a member of the health care delivery team. As future Physician Assistants we pledge to treat everyone with respect and compassion regardless of background by prioritizing compassion, quality, and continuity of care.

name: Stanford University Physics Society
description: Stanford Society of Physics Students (SUPS) aims to provide both social and academic support to the physics community at Stanford. SUPS organizes events throughout the year from regular study nights to informal faculty lunches for the undergraduate physics community. SUPS also serves as the official liason from the undergraduate physics community to the physics department.

name: Stanford University Postdoctoral Association
description: The mission of the Stanford University Postdoctoral Association is to enrich the Postdoctoral experience at Stanford, to enable Postdoctoral Scholars to explore opportunities, and to empower Postdoctoral Scholars to become leaders in areas of their choice. The Council represents and advocates for the best interests of all Stanford Postdoctoral Scholars. Primary goals of the Council include the following: 1. name: Stanford Venture Capital Club
description: SVCC provides members with an opportunity to learn more about the venture capital and entrepreneurship industries, while deepening ties with the startup ecosystem in the Bay Area and beyond.

name: Stanford Video Game Association
description: Social Gaming: SVGA endeavors to bring the Stanford community together through social video gaming in the form of in-person LAN parties, on and off campus gaming events, and campus-wide game nights. Competitive Gaming: SVGA will tryout, organize, and manage competitive teams representing Stanford in any intercollegiate or similar competitions. The processes for competitive team tryouts will be determined on a per-game and per-competition basis. Educational Gaming: SVGA will promote educational opportunities revolving around video game design. This includes, but is not limited to, exploring the

name: Stanford Vietnamese Student Association
description: Founded in 1988, Stanford Vietnamese Student Association (SVSA) seeks to share its rich cultural heritage with the campus community and foster the development of social and cultural ties with the greater Bay Area community.

name: Stanford Wind Symphony
description: To provide a forum for students, staff, and the community to practice and perform traditional and contemporary Wind Symphony music.

name: Stanford Wine Society
description: The Stanford Wine Society aims to bridge the aesthetic appreciation of wine and the academic studies of Stanford students in the natural and social sciences. For those new to wine, our group provides a welcoming, accessible introduction to wine appreciation; for those already enthusiastic about wine, we provide an environment for deeper inquiry, with a special emphasis on academic topics not explored by most conventional wine-tasting societies.

name: Stanford Women Association of Physician-Scientists
description: SWAPS is dedicated to promoting the role of women in science by supporting the personal and professional development of students in the Stanford Medical Scientist Training Program (MSTP) through longitudinal mentorship and career development opportunities.

name: Stanford Women in Bioengineering
description: Stanford Women in Bioengineering (SWIBE)'s mission is to develop a group of women on campus interested in building a community centered around the common interest of bioengineering and its role in society and our lives.

name: Stanford Women in Business
description: Stanford Women in Business was co-founded in the fall of 2005 by four Stanford undergraduate women. Today, members are supported with meaningful career direction, professional network development, and opportunities for growth. We do this by engaging with our members around three pillars: education, community, and networking. These core values form the basis of our events throughout the year—from skill development workshops to leadership conferences, career exposes, mentorship programs, speaker series, and more.

name: Stanford Women in Design
description: Our goal at Stanford Women in Design is to equip designers with tangible skills and real connections that will serve them long after they leave Stanford. SWID aims to empower women in design and champion a stronger design community on campus. We are a home for the dreamers, the makers, and the innovators. We design the world we want to live in.

name: Stanford Women in Finance
description: To empower Stanford female-identifying students to pursue careers in the financial services industry, while fostering a sense of community among members.

name: Stanford Women in Investing
description: Stanford Women in Investing aims to empower every woman, no matter their background, with the skills to become financially literate and to invest.

name: Stanford Women in Law
description: Stanford Women in Law (SWIL) aims to inspire, empower, and support women pursuing careers in law by fostering a community of passionate and engaged members. Through a combination of pre-professional activities, social justice advocacy, public service, networking, and community building, we work to prepare members for a successful career engaging with issues in the legal space and beyond.

name: Stanford Women in Medicine
description: SWIM aims to provide guidance and information to Stanford undergraduates interested in pursuing careers pertaining to medicine and health. Specifically, we aim to reach out to women in leadership positions in medically related fields as a means of inspiring Stanford undergraduate students to close the gender gap currently seen in leadership roles in medicine.

name: Stanford Women in National Security
description: Stanford Women in National Security is a pre-professional community to support young women interested in disciplines related to national security. This organization strives to connect undergraduate women with career opportunities, networking events, and mentorship bonds in the National Security field. This team further strives to provide funding an opportunities for women to pursue competition and personal projects in National Security such as the Cyber 9/12 competition.

name: Stanford Women in Politics
description: Stanford Women in Politics (SWIP) is a community of Stanford students with the mission to encourage female participation in the political process, connect individuals with the support and the mentorship to pursue their political endeavors, and provide broader political education to Stanford students to empower them to feel confident as experts on political issues.

name: Stanford Women in Tech Entrepreneurship
description: 1. Create a community of aspiring tech entrepreneurs, builders, and venture capitalists 2. Connect our members with Silicon Valley luminaries and future mentors 3. Empower members to build their own personal projects and startups

name: Stanford XR
description: Stanford XR is dedicated to advancing the outreach and development of virtual reality, augmented reality, and mixed reality at Stanford University. Our mission is to foster a diverse and inclusive community for students passionate about exploring and innovating within immersive technologies.

name: Student Interest Group in Neurology
description: To inform medical and PA students who are members of the Student Interest Group in Neurology (SIGN) of relevant classes/seminars, events, symposia, conferences, scholarships, research opportunities, and other educational or advocacy-based activities in the field.

name: Student National Medical Association
description: The Stanford Medical School Student National Medical Association (SNMA) chapter is committed to eliminating health disparities by working to increase diversity at the Stanford University School of Medicine, reaching out to underserved populations through community service, and strengthening the pipeline through from college student to medical student to house staff to attending physician. The Stanford Chapter strives to work with fellow students, faculty, and administrators to foster a more diverse environment that is enriching, encouraging, and embracing to all Stanford Medical School student

name: Students for a Sustainable Stanford
description: Students for a Sustainable Stanford is an inclusive and intersectional community that strives for long-lasting sustainable practices on and off the Stanford campus through discussion, engagement, and direct action.

name: Support and Awareness for Survivors of Human Trafficking
description: We are committed to educating the Stanford community about the silent/ hidden crisis of human trafficking both in the local Palo Alto community as well as the surrounding Bay Area. Through this organization, we hope to teach our peers the necessary skills to tap into their roles as students and advocates for our local communities. We aim to create opportunities for Stanford students interested in getting involved with social justice and community service through projects, lecture series, and workshops.

name: Sustainability Professionals and Researchers' Network
description: The Sustainability Professionals and Researchers’ Network (SPARK) aims to foster intradepartmental community building across Stanford’s Doerr School of Sustainability PhD student population. Its goal is to encourage multidisciplinary and collaborative solutions by bringing students together through both professional and social networking events, thus creating opportunities for meaningful community engagement.

name: Swingtime
description: Swingtime is Stanford's premiere performance-based swing dance troupe. Our specialty is Savoy-style Lindy Hop, a style of swing born in late-'20s Harlem. We work with professional choreographers, dance historians, and dance legends to recreate swing-era dances and integrate current trends. Swingtime's repertoire ranges from smooth swing with sleek moves to fast-paced Lindy Hop with jaw-dropping aerials. We are continually pressing the limits of how smooth, fast, and high we can go!

name: Syrian Student Association
description: To foster a community for undergraduate and graduate Syrian students, as well as students interested in ancient and modern Syrian culture at Stanford. To host a space for socialization and cultural engagement and discussion. Help Syrian students to integrate within the Stanford environment.

name: Taiwanese Cultural Society
description: The Taiwanese Cultural Society at Stanford University celebrates and promotes the rich cultural heritage of Taiwan at Stanford and the greater San Francisco Bay Area. With a diverse group of members, we work with other cultural organizations on campus to help host a variety of events including Taste of Taiwan and Iron Chef. TCS' largest event is hosting the annual Stanford Night Market!

name: Talisman
description: We are Talisman A Cappella. We were founded on Stanford's campus with an original intention of using music to shed light on underrepresented narratives, especially the music and stories of the Anti-Apartheid movement in South Africa. Every year, as Talisman recreates itself with new voices, we cull the stories that have moved us and formed us, building an ever-expanding repertoire that reflects what is most meaningful to us as individuals and as an ensemble. Talisman has had the privilege to perform at several Bay Area Schools, tour in communities in California, the East Coast, the American So

name: TAMID at Stanford
description: TAMID Group at Stanford seeks to provide students with hands-on business experience through consulting with Israeli startups and managing an equity investment portfolio. As part of the broader TAMID Group, an international organization with over 60 chapters globally, TAMID at Stanford is committed to fostering professional development, global business expertise, and a collaborative, inclusive community that enriches both academic and professional journeys.

name: Tau Beta Pi
description: The California Gamma chapter of Tau Beta Pi at Stanford University serves the Stanford community by acting as a representative entity for academic excellence, leadership, and continued service to our community. Tau Beta Pi is the only engineering honor society representing the entire engineering profession. Founded at Lehigh University by Edwards H. Williams, Jr., in 1885, Tau Beta Pi is the nation's second oldest honor society recognizing students of exemplary character and distinguished scholarship. Across the U.S., there are 248 collegiate chapters, 45 active alumni chapters in 16 districts

name: Testimony A Cappella
description: Testimony Christian A Cappella strives to spread God's love and His Word through song. We also aim to foster a warm and welcoming community.

name: Thai Student Association
description: 1. To promote Thai culture to the Stanford community through cultural and academic events. 2. To foster the relationship among Thai people at Stanford and the Bay Area. 3. To be a point of contact for those who wish to connect with Thai students at Stanford. 4. To help graduating Stanford students who wish to work in Thailand connect with working professionals through the Stanford Alumni Club of Thailand (SACOT).

name: The Bridge Peer Counseling Center
description: The Bridge Peer Counseling Center is Stanford's student run peer-counseling center. We offer anonymous and confidential 24/7 counseling to members of the greater Stanford community. Staffed by trained undergraduate and graduate Stanford students, we are here to listen and support. It is our belief that people have the fundamental ability to help and support others through personal interaction. We offer this interaction through peer counseling and support in an effort to guide those in need to develop their own solutions to problems. We are here to listen, to explore feelings, to help sort out

name: The Charles R. Blyth Fund
description: The Charles R. Blyth Fund has been managing a donation from the Blyth family since 1979, with the fund being created in December 1978. The group offers a unique, hands-on opportunity to learn about equity research and portfolio management. The membership is open to all Stanford undergraduates.

name: The Design Kids
description: The Design Kids is a co-ed, student-run design studio. We provide design services to student organizations, departments, and the administration at Stanford in an effort to facilitate portfolio development through real-world design projects as well as nurture community amongst students with a passion for design. Initiatives: 1) Nurture a tight-knit co-ed design community at Stanford + bring together the design UG and graduate communities 2) Increase the presence of design on Stanford’s campus 3) Facilitate student growth through portfolio-building projects 4) Establish long-term design partners

name: The Dish on Science
description: The mission of The Dish on Science is to increase STEM education and awareness amongst the general public. We aim to make science fun and accessible to all individuals by regularly publishing blog posts about scientific topics, answering the general public's questions about science, and engaging in community outreach.

name: The Forest
description: The Stanford Forest is the symbol of unity between students and athletes at Stanford University. We intend to build upon the tradition of success in Stanford Athletics by enhancing the fan experience and promoting a culture of student engagement and support. The Forest's mission is to conduct that which will add additional meaning to, and excitement for, Stanford's athletic programs. In coordination with the Office of Student Engagement, the Forest is chartered to fulfill that mission, in general, and to act as the defenders of all things Stanford.

name: The Science Bus
description: Stanford Science Bus is an outreach program led by graduate students from across departments. We operate an after-school program to inspire enthusiasm about science and provide mentorship from scientists. Through our partnership with East Palo Alto Charter School (EPACS), we teach hands-on science to grades 2-6 to encourage and inspire passion for engaging in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics).

name: the Stanford Alt. Protein Project
description: The Stanford Alt. Protein Project strives to build a healthy, sustainable, and ethical food system by creating a diverse, inclusive, and impact-driven community for alternative protein education, research, innovation, and awareness.

name: The Stanford Bicycle Project
description: The Stanford Bicycle Project is a registered community-service organization at Stanford University focused on promoting bicycle safety, sustainability and self-reliance. Founded in 2015, the Stanford Bicycle Project represents a strong team of student-mechanics who are passionate about cycling, engineering and helping their community. Originally endowed with a focus on both holding free bicycle repair classes and repairing abandoned bicycles for donation, the Stanford Bicycle Project has since expanded to include a partnership with the Parent's Club and FLIP to repair and distribute bicycles t

name: The Stanford Daily
description: The Stanford Daily is the independent, student-run newspaper of Stanford University. The Daily was originally founded as a small pamphlet known as The Daily Palo Alto in 1892 and has been a campus fixture ever since. The Daily strives to serve the Stanford community with relevant, unbiased journalism and provides its editorial, tech and business staffs with unparalleled educational opportunities.

name: The Stanford Flipside
description: The Stanford Flipside is a weekly satirical newsletter. Our stories are fictional, but we make jokes about real issues. Our goal is not to offend you, but to make you laugh and to reframe our world to point out the absurdities. Anyone is free to join The Flipside, and we would love to have you. We meet Tuesdays at 8:30pm in Old Union 113 to brainstorm.

name: The Stanford French Club
description: This association based at Stanford has three main objectives: 1) To facilitate contact between students of French origin, francophones, and those interested in French culture at Stanford, through a variety of events. 2) To inform students at French universities about study opportunities at Stanford and provide guidance on how to apply. 3) To promote French culture and stimulate the interest of Stanford students who might be interested in studying abroad, in undertaking French language and culture studies, or in working in France.

name: The Stanford Optical Society
description: The Stanford Optical Society aims to: • Promote awareness of optics and optical engineering among the academic and local communities • Encourage interaction and the exchange of ideas between Stanford students and the greater optics community • Serve as a means of communication and interaction between students, faculty, staff, and administration • Establish interaction between Stanford students and the Optical Society of America (OSA) and SPIE, the International Society for Optics and Photonics • Broaden student awareness of post-graduation opportunities in optics and photonics.

name: Themed Entertainment Association at Stanford University
description: The Stanford Themed Entertainment Association (STEA) aims to provide students who are interested in the industry with ride design competitions, speaker series with industry professionals, educational trips to theme parks where we meet with mentors, and a chance to build relationships with other themed entertainment loving students. We want to provide REAL, THEMED, and IMMERSIVE experiences to students on-campus to give them fun, engaging, and education adventures throughout their time at Stanford and strengthen their communities.

name: Tibetan Student Union
description: The Stanford Tibetan Student Union fosters a supportive community for Tibetan students (and friends!) and promotes awareness of Tibetan culture and issues through human rights discussions, documentary screenings, and celebrations of traditional holidays.

name: Tikkun Olam Makers
description: Tikkun Olam Makers (TOM), translated to “repair the world,” prototypes and creates open-source, affordable, assistive technology solutions to meet the neglected needs of the disabled, youth, and elderly in our local communities. By extending this mission onto Stanford’s campus, we will foster student-faculty relationships to build high-quality technology while developing the knowledge, skills, and disposition to learn from and serve our partners. At TOM, we believe in a holistic approach: link the heart, head, and hands to develop impact-driven solutions.

name: Traction Modern Dance Company
description: Traction will provide a physical and creative space for modern dancers to practice their medium and to exercise and grow choreographic skills as a group. The group will foster a collaborative community of modern dancers and will create opportunities for the campus to experience the modern dance tradition through performances and open dance workshops.

name: TreeHacks
description: We organize Stanford University's premier intercollegiate hackathon. Our mission is to bring talented students together and hack for the future.

name: Undergraduate Student National Dental Association
description: The mission of the USNDA is to aid in increasing the number of minority students entering dental schools, increasing the knowledge of dentistry in undergraduate students, and in improving DAT scores of pre-dental undergraduates. Additionally, the USNDA will provide students with the opportunity to visit dental schools and to shadow dentists, as well as to inform students of summer programs and dental research experiences. Records will also be kept of those members accepted into various dental schools.

name: United Nations Association of the United States of America Stanford University Chapter
description: UNA-USA Stanford aims to strengthen support for the United Nations while providing opportunities within the United Nations to the Stanford Community.

name: United Students for Veterans' Health
description: "To aid in the care and enrichment of veterans' lives across the nation. Ultimately, we endeavor to bring USVH to every VA Hospital in the nation to foster relationships between collegiate volunteers and patients who have given so much to our country."

name: Veritas@Stanford
description: Our mission is to foster conversations about the biggest questions we as individuals and as a society can ask. We achieve this by sustainably hosting public events where the Christian worldview is put in dialogue with other perspectives in a context of mutual respect and shared pursuit of wisdom.

name: Viennese Ball Committee
description: The Viennese Ball Committee is the team that plans the Viennese Ball and ensures that it runs smoothly. We are a group of Stanford students who are passionate about dance, operations and management, and elegant affairs. Our mission is to organize and execute the annual Viennese Ball, which usually takes place during Winter Quarter of the academic year, and in so doing, disseminate Austrian culture to the Stanford community and host an event which brings together the Stanford social dance community.

name: Vox Clara: A Journal of Christian Thought at Stanford
description: To provide a platform for believers and non-believers at Stanford to engage in dialogue that explores the role of religion in their lives and that inspires a lasting response to the Gospel message.

name: Women and Medicine
description: Women and Medicine (WAM)'s mission is to organize events and mobilize resources within the Stanford community to support women pursuing a career in medicine and to promote awareness in the medical and university community about gender disparities in medicine.

name: Women and Youth Supporting Each Other
description: WYSE shares an expansive role in educating young girls through mentorship and leadership at a local middle school.

name: Women in Aeronautics and Astronautics
description: Promote connections and opportunities for and empower marginalized genders in the aeronautics and astronautics fields. Open to all gender minorities and allies who are Stanford students and interested in aerospace.

name: Women in Computer Science
description: We are Stanford Women in Computer Science, the premier student organization dedicated to empowering & supporting our community of women in technology through community events, speaker series, recruiting events, tours, and more!

name: Women in Electrical Engineering
description: Stanford Women in Electrical Engineering (WEE) student group was founded in 2004 and has grown in size and departmental involvement throughout the years. The organization has fostered a sense of community among female EE students through programming that includes industry panels, community service events, outreach and study breaks. In addition, WEE has provided opportunities for professional development and networking across all of the engineering disciplines. name: XTRM
description: XTRM is Stanford’s non-audition K-pop dance team, dedicated to all who are passionate about dance and Korean pop culture. We teach open workshops, put on public performances, and strive to foster a community where we can engage in and enjoy K-pop choreography together.
